v0.5.7-beta.2v0.5.7-beta.2 — VoiceStudio Prerelease2026-10-23T23:10:18Z

Installer signing

Platform Signing
macOS (Apple Silicon) ✅ Signed with Developer ID and notarized by Apple
macOS (Intel) ✅ Signed with Developer ID and notarized by Apple
Windows x64 ⚠️ Unsigned: SmartScreen shows "Windows protected your PC"; choose More info → Run anyway
Windows ARM64 ⚠️ Unsigned: SmartScreen shows "Windows protected your PC"; choose More info → Run anyway
Linux x64 — Linux packages are not code-signed

Highlights

  • Preview iOS and Android apps that run VoiceStudio on your phone, offline after downloading the models
  • Opt-in Beta update channel: get fixes early from Settings → Updates, and roll onto the next stable release automatically

Changed

  • The sidebar is a slim icon rail beside each section's own pane: Home and Clone get a Saved voices / Recent takes column, Design gets a Saved voices tab, and the full navigation is one click away (#3234)

  • The GitHub button in the top bar is one Star pill with the live count, and the star fills gold on hover (#3234)

  • Stories, Audiobook and Dubbing show their saved projects in a Projects tab beside the controls, so your files are one tap away wherever you work (#3234)

  • Source ZIPs and tarballs omit scam-moderation attack examples; Git clones and CI retain their regression tests (#3237)

  • Maintainers can upload public source ZIPs or individual files with make virustotal, or scan a branch through the manual VirusTotal Actions workflow (#3237)

  • Small models now install with as little as 2 GB spare disk; the setup check only warns below 10 GB instead of blocking (#2969)

  • iOS Home shows Electron's contributor avatars, Dub is redesigned around one source card with animated icons, and the iOS bottom dock is icon-only (#2969)

  • Model licence review on iOS and Android opens with a plain summary, rights rows and licence links; the raw terms move under Exact terms (#2969)

  • Phone apps now use the app ID sh.voicestudio.mobile; a preview build installed before installs alongside as a new app, so pair it again and remove the old one (#3194)

Added

  • The phone apps run speech, dictation, voice cloning and dubbing on the phone itself, offline once you download the models; pairing a computer is optional (guide) (#2969)

  • Beta update channel: choose Stable or Beta under Settings → Updates; betas are -beta.N prereleases that never reach Stable users, and Docker gets matching :beta tags (guide) (#3175)

  • Preview iOS and Android companion apps: drive your own VoiceStudio from your phone (speak, voices and cloning, dubbing, dictation) after pairing by QR code; build from source for now (guide) (#2965)

  • Smart Fit speed limits: set the fastest and slowest speed dubbing may apply to a line, from the Timing section (#3026) — thanks @MoonDragon-MD!

Fixed

  • Saved dub loads confirm before replacing unsaved work, recheck edits made during loading and stop when you leave the workspace (#3234)

  • Large VirusTotal uploads upgrade the documented legacy upload URL to HTTPS before sending files or credentials (#3238)

  • iPhone: tapping Play right after generating speech starts playback instead of doing nothing (#3233)

  • Android app icons preserve transparent waveform paths from the shared logo, including themed icons (#2969)

  • Speak keeps your script when switching between the phone and computer on Android (#2969)

  • Phone dubbing no longer speaks the wrong words when a quiet reference clip is not recognised (#2969)

  • Refined iOS navigation, voice libraries, grouped creation forms and licence sheets with native controls, accessible text and explicit cancellation (#2969)

  • Phone apps open on an Electron-style Home dashboard with shared artwork, workspace shortcuts, recent audio, saved voices and resumable dubbing projects (#2969)

  • Phone video dubbing uses a supported AAC bitrate and preserves playable audio, rotation and synthetic-audio metadata (#2969)

  • Phone dub playback restores sound after dictation on iOS and keeps the video visible when switching results on Android (#2969)

  • Stereo reference files and dictation inputs keep both channels when converted to mono on iOS (#2969)

  • Android dubbing errors remain visible when worker updates arrive while their receipt is being saved (#3031)

  • iOS reserves storage across simultaneous model downloads and keeps saved speech paired with the submitted text (#2969)

  • TestFlight builds prepare the on-device inference runtimes before archiving the iPhone app (#2969)

  • Phone models can be reaccepted offline without downloading again, and Android dubbing preserves short audio gaps and overlaps (#2969)

  • App icon, tray icons and in-app logo no longer show a black band behind the waveform (#3221)

  • Speed/quality changes finish as soon as they are saved, even while the clone controls are still loading (#3031)

  • Speed / quality in the sidebar is a simple slider again; models and hardware fit open in a popover on hover, click or change, so the simplest view leaves the sidebar bottom free (#3031)

  • The Latest take panel is more compact: file details, render time and Check audio share one row (#3031)

  • The sidebar's Saved voices and Recent takes buttons both keep their labels instead of collapsing the inactive one to an icon (#3031)

  • On macOS full screen the sidebar logo moves into the freed corner, the compact rail drops its traffic-light gap (#3031)

  • Bug reports no longer risk freezing the app while looking for your tools: the Node-version folder scan now runs off the main thread (#3180)

  • Bug reports no longer freeze the app when the tool search or a drive stalls, and free disk is only borrowed from a parent folder when the install folder doesn't exist yet (#3179)

  • Model licence dialog is wider and scrolls as one area with the buttons pinned, and follows macOS, Windows and Linux dialog conventions (#3160)

  • Bug reports now include your OS, memory, free disk and whether the Python runtime exists, even when the backend never started, plus flags for risky install paths such as OneDrive or non-ASCII folders (#3156)

  • Bug reports no longer hang on a stalled drive, and report free disk and the uv tool correctly on first run and in source checkouts (#3170)

  • Older synthesized takes play again with accurate play/pause controls after a newer generation (#3102)

  • Generation-complete notifications appear above the workspace instead of covering synthesis controls (#3102)

  • Generated speech no longer starts and ends with silence, and [pause] markers give exactly the pause you asked for (Raw preset and explicit durations untouched) (#3080)

  • Engine sidecars no longer load PyTorch just to answer the Test Engine ping, and a failed test logs its reason locally (#3026) — thanks @tekay-de!

Fixed

  • Windows runtime refresh no longer fails with EPERM on a locked backend folder (OneDrive, antivirus): it updates the files in place; the missing-Python-environment message now names the exact folder and tells non-checkout installs to use the installer (#3023) — thanks @afraniohugo, @javalovelinux-cmd and @eduardpp00!

Fixed

  • The install location chosen in first-run setup now also holds your data, model cache and temp files instead of quietly filling C:, and the setup screen shows each path (#2971, #3035)

  • Supertonic-3's preset voices can be picked in the voice controls and are used for generation (#2938, #3035)

  • OMNIVOICE_ENGINES_DIR moves engine venvs and the audio.cpp runtime to another drive; the default location is unchanged (#3024)

Fixed

  • The installed app now rebuilds a Python environment that antivirus or disk cleanup removed, once per launch with the usual setup progress, instead of stopping at a setup error; your voices and projects are untouched (#3032) — thanks @afraniohugo and @javalovelinux-cmd!

Changed

  • The sponsor footer is gone from the app; sponsored integrations keep a Featured badge on their card in Integrations (#3031)

Docs

  • SPONSORS.md now states what each sponsorship tier gives, when recognition starts, and what sponsorship does not buy, and the README and inquiry form point to it (#3172)
  • OmniVoice GGUF docs state that the installers do not ship its native binary yet (#3026) — thanks @DestinyQJY!
  • Contributor guides and the pull request template explain how to sign the CLA before opening a first pull request (#2676)

Fixed

  • macOS builds without a Developer ID are now signed ad hoc so the bundle signature is valid, and the shell installer clears quarantine, repairs an invalid signature of older releases, names an unreadable disk image, and tells Intel Mac users the backend needs Apple Silicon (#3033, #2763, #2829, #2681)
  • A "Generation failed" log line now says where it was raised and which error caused it, and the out-of-memory advice mentions picking another GPU, so these reports can be told apart (#2895, #2684, #2666, #2626, #2622, #2580, #3034)

CI

  • Release notes list everyone who contributed since the last stable release automatically, instead of only the people thanked by hand (#3242)

  • Release notes list each platform's installer signing as measured on the build, and a macOS build that would open as "damaged" can no longer be released, and macOS releases are signed with the Developer ID again (#3241, #3243)

  • The owner can let named maintainers publish releases while Windows installers are still unsigned (#3236)

  • Android release and Play builds share an increasing version code to prevent reused or decreasing build numbers (#2969)

  • Phone build resources keep notice hashes and localized text intact on Windows (#2969)

  • New mobile-release workflow builds signed Android and iOS apps and drafts a GitHub prerelease with the APK, AAB and IPAs (#2969)

  • The mobile workflow builds the pinned on-device runtimes for both apps (#2969)

  • The main test step runs in parallel with pytest-xdist, about 3 minutes faster per CI run (#3223)

  • Interactive release helper: pick stable or beta, draft or publish, and confirm by typing the tag (scripts/release.py) (#3187)

  • Release helper choices are arrow-key menus (#3190)

  • Desktop UI tests no longer fail at random when Electron's debugger takes the dev proxy's port; the proxy now binds an OS-assigned port (#3126)

  • Desktop request-guard self-tests stay deterministic when app requests arrive during cleanup (#2676)

  • New mobile workflow builds and tests both phone apps; a contract test fails when their theme or API description drifts from the desktop app (#2965)

  • iOS TestFlight workflow: maintainers can upload a signed iPhone build for internal testers from main (guide) (#3188)

  • iOS TestFlight builds declare their exempt encryption, so uploads no longer wait on the export compliance question (#3230)

  • iOS TestFlight uploads with on-device inference pass App Store validation, and the workflow checks every bundled framework before uploading (#3235)

  • Beta and stable release builds no longer fail when a slow build machine runs the app's tests (#3232)

  • Android Play internal testing workflow: the matching signed Android upload from main, and beta versions no longer break the Android build (guide) (#3189)

  • Gallery preview fallback smoke no longer flakes when a slower runner reads the playing clip in several byte ranges (#3018)

Contributors

Thanks to everyone who contributed to this release: @debpalash, @velixio, @rudycelekli, @swadhinbiswas, @kevin9327, @nvtoan0201-swe, @nirmalchatur, @BichengWang, @chiarorosa, @emreisik95, @abdullah-rashid62, @drakeo338, @FenjuFu, @Vaishnavi220506, @Nikhi00718, @shivsin25, @bercedev, @Cengokill, @DeryFerd, @ege-arhan, @eltociear, @HoneyTyagii, @li-lizhe, @mvanhorn, @NN708, @Raunaksplanet, @vincentfranstyo, @JoshuaWIls, @strauss-visuals, @Yi-111-a

Imbad0202/academic-research-skills ↗ 1 release · 1 stable
v3.23.2v3.23.2 — Integrity checks read only the cited version, Stage 2.5 always runs, and adapter, announce, and Windows repairs Stable2026-10-24T13:43:28Z

Repairs; no new skill. One prompt-level change has a small behaviour check, and the others are unmeasured: v3.23.2 makes the Stage 2.5 and 4.5 claim checks compare a claim only with the version of a work that the manuscript cites (#1006). When that version cannot be read, the check records an access note and asks for its PDF instead of reading a working paper or preprint. In one synthetic fixture run six times (three sessions each on Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Fable 5.1, web tools off), every session followed the rule. A prior integrity report no longer lets a pipeline run skip Stage 2.5; the run attaches it as context (#995). A missing required input blocks the stage transition on every surface (#990), and the Socratic mentor's example no longer ranks the user's ideas (#992). The SessionStart announce shows the update reminder to the user, and the model-facing announce is about 2.1 KB shorter (#999). The Obsidian adapter accepts unquoted ISO dates and rejects boolean and superscript-digit years (#988, #989); six lints compare paths in POSIX form on Windows (#964, #978); the Pi wrapper composes with Pi's structured prompt sections (#985); and CITATION.cff gives the author's ORCID iD (#1007). Outside contributors wrote #978, #985, and #988.

Changed

  • CITATION.cff gives the author's ORCID iD (#1007). Zenodo reads the file when it archives a release, so later versions under the concept DOI link their creator to https://orcid.org/0009-0008-9523-0103. Versions already on Zenodo do not change.

Fixed

  • The SessionStart announce shows the user what is meant for the user (#999). scripts/announce-ars-loaded.sh sent everything through additionalContext, which reaches only the model, so the #544 update reminder never reached the user. Startup and clear now also set systemMessage: a one-line loaded notice, preceded by the update reminder when one is available. The model-facing startup announce replaces the 16-row command table, the agent table, and the token-budget line with one line of command names and one line of agent names (about 2.1 KB less per session); the command-invariants lint still checks every /ars-* token and the count. The skill-routing paragraph and the routing core are unchanged. Three tests in scripts/test_ars_update_check.py pin the new field.
  • Missing required inputs block the transition in the pipeline state machine too (#990). The Missing Materials section of academic-pipeline/references/pipeline_state_machine.md let the user "skip (at own risk)" a required input, while shared/handoff_schemas.md Validation Rules (rule 5) and the state tracker's gap table block the transition. The section now follows the state tracker: a missing required input returns HANDOFF_INCOMPLETE and is backfilled before the next stage runs, a missing recommended input does not block and is reported, and integrity checks still cannot be skipped. The #528 content lock is updated.
  • The Socratic mentor's "direct answer" example no longer ranks the user's ideas (#992). The example in deep-research/agents/socratic_mentor_agent.md said "your second idea actually has a lot of potential", which the Research-Question Authorship Boundary in the same file forbids. It now declines and asks which of the user's own directions they most want to understand, and why. The ideation-diversity non-production variant pins the new source hash. Prompt-level; the effect on model behaviour is unmeasured.
  • A prior integrity report no longer lets a pipeline run skip Stage 2.5 (#995). shared/handoff_schemas.md Validation Rules (rule 11) and the academic-pipeline/SKILL.md Mid-Entry Protocol allowed a fresh, unmodified, user-confirmed report to skip Stage 2.5, while the orchestrator's Mid-Entry Material Passport Check required Stage 2.5 in every run and attached the prior report as context. All surfaces now follow the orchestrator: Stage 2.5 always runs before Stage 3, and a prior report that is VERIFIED, fresh, and on the current version is attached to the run as context. The same rule is stated in the orchestrator's mid-entry routing rules and the Stage 3 row of academic-pipeline/references/mode_advisor.md. check_spec_consistency.py pins the new rule-11 heading and body and the absence of the old skip wording in the four files; the #528 content locks are updated. Prompt-level; the effect on model behaviour is unmeasured.
  • Phase E checks a claim only against the version of a work that the manuscript cites (#1006). Stage 2.5 and 4.5 source tracing (academic-pipeline/references/claim_verification_protocol.md E2, mirrored in integrity_verification_agent.md) could read a working paper or preprint when the cited version was not readable, and judge the claim against it, which produced both false flags and false passes. The check now identifies the cited version from the reference entry (and from version_records.yaml when present), never substitutes another version, and records UNVERIFIABLE_ACCESS with a request for the cited version's PDF when that version cannot be read, including an open-access page the agent cannot read. A reference entry that does not identify exactly one version gets the same note with VERSION_INCONSISTENT_CITATION, and an author-accepted manuscript stands in only when the reference cites it. For a claim with several sources, an access note on one source no longer hides a distortion found in another. Each evidence row names the version in its existing source.display_label, which the rendered table already prints; the evidence-row schema does not change. The orchestrator's checkpoint line asks for the cited version's PDF (content lock updated). check_evidence_row_integration.py pins the rules, and scripts/test_phase_e_cited_version.py pins that the row carrier records and renders the access outcome. Whether runs follow the rule is prompt-level. In one synthetic fixture run six times (three sessions each on Claude Opus 5.5 and Claude Fable 5.1, web tools off), every session recorded the access note, asked for the cited version, and issued no verdict from the working paper that was readable.
  • The Obsidian adapter rejects a boolean year and a year written in superscript digits (#989). _coerce_year in scripts/adapters/obsidian.py accepted year: true as an integer, because bool is a subclass of int, and wrote year: true to the corpus. A year string such as '²⁰²⁴' passed str.isdigit() and then raised ValueError in int(), which stopped the run before the passport was written. Both notes are now rejected with year_unparseable and the run continues. The string check uses str.isdecimal(), so years in other decimal scripts that int() reads are still accepted. A parametrized test in scripts/adapters/tests/test_obsidian.py covers both cases.
  • The Obsidian adapter accepts a year written as an unquoted ISO date (#987, #988, contributed by @harshajv7981). yaml.safe_load turns year: 2024-01-15 into a datetime.date before _coerce_year sees it, so the adapter rejected the note as year_unparseable, although its docstring lists that form as accepted; Obsidian's Properties panel writes Date properties this way. _coerce_year now takes the year from a date or datetime value. A regression test in scripts/adapters/tests/test_obsidian.py covers it.
  • The Pi wrapper composes ARS with Pi's structured prompt sections (#966, #985, contributed by @daniyyell-dev). When the wrapper returned a rendered systemPrompt, Pi treated it as a complete override and could drop sections from other extensions, such as MCP instructions. When event.systemPromptOptions is available, the wrapper now filters package-owned skills while ARS is inactive and adds an ars_compatibility section while it is active; stopping ARS removes only that section. Hosts without the structured API keep the string and array fallback from #880. Unit tests and an opt-in integration test against Pi 1.1.0 and 1.3.0 cover it.
  • Windows: six lints compare repository paths in POSIX form (#964, #978, contributed by @daniyyell-dev). check_684_review_criteria_binding.py, check_collaboration_depth_rubric.py, check_content_coverage_advisory_integration.py, check_cross_document_consistency_advisory_integration.py, check_decision_contract.py, and check_tortured_phrase_screening_integration.py compared str(Path), which uses \ on Windows, with forward-slash paths, and failed on a correct tree. They now use Path.as_posix(). The new tests pass Windows-style paths into each lint's comparison, so the Ubuntu CI fails if a conversion is reverted.

code-yeongyu/oh-my-openagent ↗ 1 release · 1 stable
v5.1.45 Stable2026-10-24T12:08:10Z

Reading the end of a long session takes 42 ms and 68 MB instead of 40 s and 1.8 GB. session_read, session_search and session_info page through OpenCode's message API instead of loading the whole session: on a 23,000-message session, session_read with limit: 2, from_end: true dropped from 39.6 s and 1,848 MB peak memory to 42 ms and 68 MB, and a search that runs out its 60-second timeout now stops reading when it returns, where it used to read another 228 MB in the background (#10738, #10741).

OmO's extension no longer carries an LSP engine it never runs. The native LSP tools and post-edit diagnostics already go through the packaged LSP daemon, but the formatter's import pulled lsp-core's whole in-process engine into omo.js; importing only the helpers it uses shrinks the extension by about 82 KB, with no change in behavior. (#10659)

Every session start reads about 33 KB less of omo.js: eleven memory slash commands and memory sync's device account load on first use (#10902, #10860). The commands (/memory, /remember, /init, /recompile, /memory-repository, /sleeptime, /reflect, /dream, /search, /facts, /agreements) still appear at startup with the same names, descriptions and hints; their handlers load from extensions/omo-memory-commands.js. The signed-in device account loads from extensions/omo-device-account.js the first time a session resolves its sync, and if that file cannot load, memory sync reports sync-unavailable with the reason instead of looking signed out.

ulw-research ships a fact ledger, a fidelity state file and a claim index for research reports. They give each research run a machine-readable record of its facts and verified claims; nothing in the CLI uses them yet. (#11046, part of #11009; batch #11148)

Child-task, workflow and workpool wake sources report kind children. (#11114, part of #10782)

An unreadable workpool store no longer drops or falsely clears the children wake source. (#11118, part of #10782)

The children wake source reads the workpool store once per snapshot. (#11124, part of #10782) (batch #11148)

Child results waiting in the wake queue keep the parent from reading as done. (#11115, part of #10782)

The wake-queue count can no longer cost a delivery receipt and is re-published per session generation. (#11121, part of #10782)

A receipt that throws no longer leaves the wake-queue count up. (#11122, part of #10782)

Delivery receipts are isolated from each other, on retire too, and no receipt error is dropped. (#11123, part of #10782) (batch #11148)

A wake-queue flush settles each receipt and the child count once, and a throwing onReceiptError no longer stops the rest. (#11137, part of #10782) (batch #11148)

Windows helper tree kills are guarded against recycled parent PIDs. A QA helper no longer stops an unrelated process tree that reused a parent's PID. (#11007)

A task that a quitting session suspended says why it is still running. Quitting the owning session parks every live child, but the parked record kept its bare running status with no reason, so a restart that never resumed that session read as a running task that nothing would ever move. The quit shutdown now records session_quit on the parked record, which task_output and the task snapshot present as "resuming (session quit)", and a later resume whose reconcile defers the revival replaces it with the deferral's own reason. (senpi#3493, #10533, thanks @Bearmancer)

A project's skills can no longer reach outside the project, and their MCP servers no longer get your whole environment. A skill link in a project that points outside it is refused, and the reason shows in the skill tool's result and in OpenCode; links into skill folders you configured yourself still work. MCP servers that come from a project's skills start with a small safe base (paths, home, temp, locale, CA paths) plus the variables they declare. When one asks for a variable it didn't get, the result names it with the exact /omo-mcp-env-grant command that saves the grant for that server declaration; only names are stored, in the same file the engine uses. Skills you installed yourself, including paths in your global OpenCode configuration, keep today's environment. Task discovery keeps nested reference documents out of skills and allows links between packages in the same repository. Unreadable or missing skills report their actual file error rather than a security block. Replaced or evicted grant commands expire, and reopening the server provides a fresh command when needed. (#10716)

Computer use explains a refused macOS launch context instead of reporting a closed engine. Initial activation and later restarts now report COMPUTER_LAUNCH_CONTEXT_REQUIRED with recovery instructions when the actual engine child refuses to start. Permission errors, desktop handover, and the native launch gate keep their existing behavior. (#11073, #11086)

Thread tools check that an RPC host is the one they selected before changing a session (#10712). The client proves the host's key with a challenge-response and attaches the selected session by its durable id on the same connection, so a host that reused a routing id cannot receive another session's mutation. A draining host answers with a retryable host_draining error instead of failing the call, and a change that took effect is never reported as failed.

The build now records which files each bundled artifact is built from. packages/omo-senpi/bundle-inputs.json lists every repo file the generators of the committed bundles read. The list is traced from the recipe itself, and CI checks that it is current. Merge tooling can now tell that a skill-only change leaves the bundles untouched (#11079, #11084).

A session with telemetry off clears leftover session summaries as soon as it starts. Summary files a crashed session left behind used to stay on disk until a later session with telemetry on picked them up. A session with telemetry off now deletes them at startup when omo.json turns telemetry off for their project; an opt-out set only through an environment variable such as DO_NOT_TRACK applies to that session alone and leaves other sessions' summaries in place. Turning telemetry off in omo.json takes effect on the very next turn instead of up to five seconds later. A summary whose project cannot be told apart is never sent. (#10234) (#10267) (batch #11148)

Session summaries survive a crash at any step and are never counted twice. Each summary window now has its own id, sent as the event id, and is written to a local pending file before it is sent; the file is deleted only after delivery is confirmed, and a later OmO start re-sends anything left over under the same id. A window left open by a killed process is sent once, only after that process is gone and its once-a-minute heartbeat has stopped for 5 minutes, so a sleeping laptop keeps its own window. The session sequence survives restarts and counts within a random per-run summary_epoch, and a session continued or recovered by another process starts a new one, so two processes writing one session never send the same (epoch, sequence) pair even when one of them is wrongly taken for dead, costs are added as whole 1/10,000 USD units (cost_1e4) so summaries and raw turns agree exactly, and dropped_events counts what had to be discarded after 14 days. telemetry.rawTurnSampleRate (or OMO_TELEMETRY_RAW_TURN_SAMPLE_RATE) sets the share of sessions that also send raw turn rows, 0.05 by default. (#10198, #10225) (batch #11148)

Every session event says whether it came from a session you opened or one OmO spawned. session_started, turn_completed and session_summary carry session_role (root, child or unknown), so a delegated child's usage is not counted again on top of its parent. (#10198, #10225) (batch #11148)

Raw turn rows keep the name of a public model reached through your own gateway. turn_completed masked the model to custom whenever the provider was not one OmO ships, while session_summary and every other event already kept a published model id regardless of the routing provider. The gateway name itself is still never sent. (#10198, #10225) (batch #11148)

Plan review keeps working after a restart or a restored session (#10558). plan-consultant and plan-reviewer only spawn after you asked for ulw-plan and a plan file exists. That state used to live only in memory, so after a restart, a desktop restore or a resumed session the gate was empty and plan review was refused until you asked again. The gate is now rebuilt from the session's own transcript when it starts: plan file reads and writes count again, and a request counts only when the engine recorded you typed it (senpi 2026.10.21-2 and later), so text injected by an extension still never opens it. State handed over by a reload is kept as well (#10378).

The engine moves to senpi 2026.10.23-1: scheduled prompts and /loop ticks reach an open session mid-turn, the footer shows what subagents spent, and compaction works again on very long sessions and turns (#11126). A scheduled prompt now arrives in its open session, steered into the running turn when the agent is working, and a /loop tick that comes due mid-turn is read at the next step. Each session remembers the thinking level per model. Stop pauses the session until you type or /resume. An HTTP MCP server with no saved sign-in no longer freezes the process for up to 30 seconds, a background usage check no longer locks a healthy Claude login on a network error, and a models.json entry without a price keeps the built-in price instead of billing $0. The built-in /llama llama.cpp integration is removed upstream; a saved llama.cpp provider is ignored.

Bun-installed omo keeps its command links intact so later upgrades can succeed. Launches still start directly on Bun, and a new-version launch restores older generated wrappers to symlinks. This fixes recurring EEXIST failures on Bun 1.4.4; the first upgrade from an old wrapper may need the one-time removal described in the PR. (#11024)

The engine moves to senpi 2026.10.21-3: long 1M-context conversations stop re-writing their cached prefix, Anthropic subscription context is counted once, and "No credential slots available" no longer locks every account out (#10965). When context reduction trims a long conversation on a 1M window, the reduced prefix now stays identical and keeps its cache checkpoint, so each step writes only what changed. Anthropic subscription turns with internal SDK re-requests no longer double the context percentage or start compaction early, and a configured compaction model now does threshold, speculative and idle compaction while your session provider is healthy. The subscription lane is the only layer that picks its accounts, so one revoked or briefly rate-limited account no longer blocks the rest until you log in again. Every turn end says what happens next, a turn-end report names the hold your queued message released, the trailing "Anything else? (optional)" card is gone from clients without native questions, and moving a session between machines runs through one implementation. Forced recovery after a context overflow no longer picks the same compaction cut again when an invisible entry leads the session; an overflow still never moves a task to its next fallback model.

Tasks honour a -fast model alias that the provider config pairs with a model. Kibitzer no longer stops at a model whose start is refused; it falls back to the next one. (#10538, fixes #10536)

Child startup failures keep their cause. When a task child exits while the parent writes to stdin, its own typed failure is reported instead of a broken-pipe error. (#11097, fixes #11096)

The side panel says, once, that its column needs the fullscreen TUI. side_panel.enabled renders its right-hand column only in the fullscreen TUI (--tui-mode fullscreen, or tuiMode in senpi's settings); in the default regular mode the sections stay a block above the editor. The docs now say so at the top of the side_panel table, and the first regular-mode run with the panel on shows a one-time notice naming both ways to switch. (#10560, #10565)

A background task that wakes itself up, or reconnects after the task host restarts, keeps the right finished/running mark on the host (#11094). A task that started a new run on its own just as its previous turn finished could stay marked as finished, so a replaced task host might drop it while it was still working. A finished task whose host restarted could lose its finished mark, so the new host might reopen it. Both now keep the correct mark. (#11092)

The side panel shows subscription usage when you are signed in but the engine is serving through an environment token (#10564). It used to show nothing in that case; it still never shows a different signed-in account's numbers. (#11101)

The one-line Linux installer picks the glibc build on glibc hosts that also have the musl package installed. install.sh used to treat any /lib/ld-musl-*.so.1 loader as proof of a musl system, so Debian or Ubuntu hosts with musl-tools or musl-dev installed downloaded omo-linux-x64-musl and recorded it for later updates. A glibc host (one where getconf GNU_LIBC_VERSION answers) now always gets the glibc build. The musl check also reads ldd --version in a way that still matches under pipefail, since musl's ldd exits 1 after printing its version. (#10562, #10612)

bun run lint runs the copy check again, and Bun no longer warns on every process in the repo. The root package.json had two "lint" scripts after a merge, so the copy check was silently skipped and Bun printed a "Duplicate key" warning to stderr each time it started, which failed tests that expect a quiet child. One lint script now runs both checks, and a test rejects repeated keys in any package.json. (#11108)

Memory notes keep their exact line endings on Windows. Git for Windows converts line endings by default, so a note committed with LF or mixed endings came back with CRLF in a reflection worktree, and the description preflight that must keep every non-description byte failed there. Every memory repository now pins core.autocrlf=false, and opening an older repository restores only the working copies whose sole difference from the committed note is the converted line endings. (#11112, fixes #11109) (batch #11148)

Memory reflection and dream runs trim oversized note descriptions before completion validation. The note body is preserved, instead of the run failing again and again and parking the identity. (#10999)

The frontend skill now decides what a screen leaves out before drawing it, and visual QA proves a redesign improved and stops after a few rounds (#11023). Before code, every screen names one primary action, its information priorities, what it leaves out on purpose, and the content it must keep; after the draft renders, a subtraction pass removes what the user does not need and checks nothing required was dropped or merged. Small changes now read the project's design file and at most one reference instead of the whole library, and atmosphere and award-grade styling are built only when the brief asks. Visual QA gains a before/after mode that captures fixed cases before the first edit and compares them side by side, and its review loop now ends after 2-3 rounds: layout, function, accessibility and missing-content defects earn another round, taste notes are recorded and stop it.

Computer use refuses input while the stop chord cannot be heard. On macOS, a password field or Secure Keyboard Entry turns on Secure Event Input, which hides key presses from the stop chord's listener; computer use kept running anyway, so the chord could not stop it. Input is now refused with StopPathUnavailable (secure-input-active) until secure input ends, and resumes by itself. A type in progress now stops at the next character when the stop path stops authorizing input, instead of finishing the text, and the Linux X11 listener refuses to arm on an XInput 2.0 server, where a keyboard grab would swallow the chord. Plain Esc stays an ordinary key. (#10534, #9651, #10537)

The frontend draft guard now catches promotional copy, emoji icons, hype badges and vanity stats, not only accent stripes (#11022). One command, check-draft-guard.ts, runs the accent-stripe rules plus four checks on visible markup text: promotional filler in English and Korean copy, an emoji used as an icon, a badge whose only content is a hype label such as "New" or "AI-powered", and a stat tile holding a marketing-form number such as "10x", "500+" or "24/7"; a measured figure such as "42%" or "1.2k" passes. Code (TypeScript generics and comparisons included), scripts, styles, comments, hidden elements, bound values and badges that carry a state attribute are not flagged. React component tags such as <Badge> and <Stat value="10x">, cn() class lists, and announced attributes such as aria-label and placeholder are checked too. The frontend and visualize skills now run it before visual QA in place of check-accent-stripes.ts, which still works on its own. Both commands now skip a dangling symlink in a scanned folder instead of crashing, and report an unreadable path given on the command line with exit 2.

A memory sync that stops working now says so in the TUI, with what to do. When a sync cycle failed, the error went only to the log, and the status kept reporting the last successful sync. Now the memory footer shows sync blocked while sync is failing, and one notice says why and what to do: /memory unlock <path> for a git lock left behind by a crashed writer, sign in again for an expired sign-in, or check your connection when the sync service cannot be reached. A single dropped request still retries quietly; the offline notice appears only after three failed cycles in a row. When sync recovers, a notice says so and the footer clears. (#10637, #10958)

Store extensions can expose session-callable ops as real tools, and their worker no longer drags a schema library into every store. A store extension's sessionCallable declaration can now carry a toolName, description and JSON Schema parameters per op: the session's engine registers it as ext_<extension>_<toolName>, the tool takes the calling session's durable id from the engine (never from arguments), and the worker stamps caller_session_durable_id and, when the caller thread_create'd the target, caller_created_target inside the op's own transaction. Args naming either caller field are refused before validation; the public extensionCall channel refuses every declared session op. The worker validates op arguments itself against a JSON Schema subset (type, properties, required, additionalProperties true/false, enum, const, pattern, length/item/number bounds, items, anyOf), and register() refuses any other keyword, so no constraint is skipped - which also removed typebox/value from the store worker: its bundle drops from 206 KB to 115 KB and every worker spawn (and idle-retire respawn) stops paying for its module graph. A declared await with statusOp/expireOp/timeoutMs arms a wake-file wait, and thread_creations records who created which session durably across host restarts. (#9551)

Product copy uses clearer punctuation instead of em dashes (#10994). Agent prompts, notices, memory recall openers, and web metadata now use commas, colons, or parentheses, and an empty-value placeholder uses a hyphen. A source AST check prevents new em dashes in product strings, template elements, and JSX text while leaving comments, regexes, tests, generated code, and vendored sources alone. The same check now requires lint and TypeScript suppressions to explain why, inline or in the comment directly above, including Biome ignores.

Inside OmO Desktop the browser skill works as in the terminal, plus the app's built-in browser. The agent's browsers (your own through BrowserSkill, or one it starts itself) are no longer refused or changed inside the app, and connectBuiltinBrowser() adds the thread's tab in the app's built-in browser, which you can watch beside the chat (#11066).

A session in the OmO desktop app's Built-in browser mode can ask the app for its in-app browser. The browser skill told the agent to use the app's in-app browser tools, but an OmO session had none, so agents reached for whatever outside browser the machine had (sisyphuslabs/omo-desktop-app#3292). A new eval-only omo_desktop_toolkit tool asks the app for a toolkit it hosts for the session's thread, and connectBuiltinBrowser() in the browser skill uses it to attach OmOWright to that thread's tab. The app's grant names a loopback endpoint and a token file, so the token never appears in a tool result; an app that offers no toolkit is answered at once, and one that does not answer within 15 s gets a timeout. Works once the desktop app ships its side. (#10602, fixes #10601)

Parked facts leave the active queue without losing their contents. Existing backlogs migrate once, manual retry restores them, and turn-end scans read only active entries. (#11038)

The side panel's usage section reads the subscription limits the engine already keeps, so it shows the same numbers as the desktop, before the first turn, and makes no network request of its own (#10553). senpi now polls each signed-in Claude and ChatGPT subscription itself (code-yeongyu/senpi#3687); the panel only picks the serving account and draws its record. A rotation to an account the engine has not read yet shows nothing rather than the previous account's numbers. side_panel.usage_poll_seconds is retired: still accepted, now ignored.

A finished background task no longer wakes up on its own after the task host restarts (#11083). A task that ran on the shared task host kept its session loaded there after it finished, with nothing saying it was done. When the host was replaced, the new host reopened it, and the task's own follow-ups could run again with nobody watching, spending usage. The task now marks its session as finished on the host as soon as it finishes, and again before it lets go, so the new host leaves it closed even if the parent session crashed. A finished task you continue with task_send is marked running again before your message is delivered; a dropped connection that reconnects does not change the mark. (#10778)

The web-terminal visual QA driver can wait for text before it types. A slow-starting TUI used to lose its first keystrokes to the fixed start delay. Put {WaitFor:<text>} in --input and the driver polls the rendered xterm buffer until <text> appears, then continues; if it never appears within --wait-for-timeout-ms (default 10000) the capture fails with an error naming the text and the timeout, and an empty {WaitFor:} is refused. Thanks to @cynkai. (#9583, #9666)

git-master credits sisyphus-dev-ai on its commits again, once per commit, and you can turn it off. Every commit git-master writes ends with Co-authored-by: sisyphus-dev-ai <sisyphus-dev-ai@users.noreply.github.com>. Git adds the trailer itself (git -c trailer.ifexists=addIfDifferent commit --trailer), so amending or rewording a commit that already carries it keeps a single copy, and after a squash git-master rewrites the joined message once. This needs git 2.32 or newer. git_master.include_co_authored_by in omo.json is a working switch again and defaults to true; set it to false to leave the trailer out. The commit footer stays opt-in, your own git author and committer are unchanged, and the GIT_MASTER=1 prefix applies to the commit command as before. This works the same in the Native harness (reading the skill or load_skills) and the OpenCode plugin (#10713, #10715).

The count of undelivered messages matches the messages actually dropped (#10987). When a stopped parent cancelled a task, or a task that could not be resumed was closed, its queued messages were dropped with a note saying how many. That count came from a read taken just before the queue was cleared, so a message sent in between was dropped without being counted. The count now comes from the same write that clears the queue. (#10866)

A relaunched task records its own session id, not the previous run's (#10985). When a task restarted on a new transcript (a model fallback or a revive) and its new session's first state read failed, the task kept the previous run's session id, so anything that looks a task up by its session id, such as the task tree or the cleanup when a parent stops, found the old session. The first id the new run learns now replaces it. (#10892)

The footer shows what your subagents are spending, live, next to the session's own cost (#10730). The session cost only counted the session itself, so the number stood still while subagents worked. The footer now adds the whole subagent tree's spend as (+$X), including nested children and revived runs, and updates as tasks report instead of polling (code-yeongyu/senpi#2471).

Subagent rows no longer show $0.0000 when the provider sent no usage (#10727). A turn whose provider streamed no usage block came back with an all-zero usage, and the task row counted it as a real $0, with no tok/s. Such a turn now counts as "cost not reported", so the row shows no amount, and a run where only some turns reported a cost is marked partial (#10724).

Internal: a telemetry spool lock this process could not delete no longer blocks its batch until the 14-day age limit. After a transient file error (for example on Windows), the sweep reclaims the lock once the claim lease has passed, while a lock for a move still in progress is kept (#10951).

Internal: every assistant turn opens one omo.turn OpenTelemetry span, and events emitted during the turn carry its trace and span ids. On a transport with a span sink (the OTLP collector transport; the PostHog transport has none) the Senpi adapter starts the span at turn_start and ends it ok, or error for a failed or abandoned turn, so a turn_completed row, its span and an error event join on the (trace_id, span_id) pair. A process child launched by the task engine continues the delegating turn's trace. The traceparent header goes only to our own hosts, never to a model provider, and nothing is started or written while telemetry is off. (#10358)

Internal: the telemetry spool recovers and bounds itself on every sweep, and a stalled sender never re-sends a batch it lost. Every live collector transport sweeps the spool on start and every 60 s: it recovers expired claims and the files of dead processes, applies the 5 MB cap to everything in the directory (not only to what it sealed itself), and replays oldest first; when consent has ended the sweep deletes the spool instead. Before every send attempt the sender renames its claim to a fresh lease, so a process that stalled past its lease and lost the batch to another process stops instead of sending it again, and a batch claimed when consent is withdrawn is deleted unsent. Nothing is wired to a product yet. (#10355)

The engine publishes its OpenTelemetry schema artifact. telemetry-schema.json describes exactly what an OTel client of the engine may send, generated from the event schemas and kept byte-exact by a drift gate, so the telemetry collector can pin and enforce it. It is separate from the anonymous PostHog events, which are unchanged (#10980).

The frontend skill picks a layout pattern for every layout change, and visual-qa checks it. Any change to a screen's structure (a new region, panel, split, list, sticky bar or scroll container) now fetches the matching StyleGallery pattern and writes one Layout: line in DESIGN.md naming the pattern, the element that owns the scroll and the pattern's anti-patterns, including in a project that already has a DESIGN.md. visual-qa's new A12 item checks the build against that line, with a probe for the element that really scrolls. Apple HIG hit targets, hierarchy, states, keyboard and motion are now rules for the first draft in the frontend skill, not only items in the QA checklist. (#10684, #10685)

New TypeScript and JavaScript projects default to oxlint and oxfmt. The programming skill now ships strict OXC configs and the t3code copy rules: product strings, templates, and JSX reject em dashes, and lint/type suppressions require an explanation. Existing repository toolchains are respected. (#11030)

Account commands no longer repeat a failed keychain operation while reporting the error. A native storage failure or timeout now returns exit 9 with {"error":"store-unavailable"} instead of attempting another store read, which could add a second 25-second wait. Existing success and locked-keychain outcomes are preserved; no new deadline or lock change is introduced (#11040, #11049).

A removed device ends its local account session on refresh. When the service refuses a renewal with device_revoked, omo account token clears the saved credential and returns exit 5 with that code; omo account show then reports signed out. Unknown refusal codes still retain the credential as uncertain (#11041, #11048).

Project memory reads work on Windows when a path uses a short user-directory name. Read grants now compare native canonical paths on both sides, accounting for Windows case and separator differences without granting sibling memory repositories. A granted repository that is later replaced by a link elsewhere is no longer covered, and a note that does not exist yet is still allowed so the read can report it missing. (#10982)

Each model family's current default is named once. Every builtin default, fallback rung, category gate, Claude Code alias and migration target that means "the newest Opus / Sonnet / Haiku / Fable / GPT / GLM / Kimi / Gemini" now reads its id from one table, so the next model bump is one edit. Resolved models stay the same, with one exception: the Claude Code sonnet alias now means the current Sonnet (claude-sonnet-5-5) instead of claude-sonnet-4-6. (#10483, #10141)

A builtin model profile can run on your own provider. When the only provider serving a profile's model is one you declared in models.json (for example an API-key proxy serving claude-opus-5-5), Daily · Normal and the other builtin lanes now pick it instead of reporting that no model is available. Only the models you declared for that provider count, the lane's own providers still come first, and gateways you never declared still never serve a builtin lane. Reported by 채완. (#10493, #10485)

/mass-ulw and run mass ulw ... now enter the mode instead of offering a pointer the model could skip. The slash command (/mass-ulw, /mulw, /ulw-research) or a prompt that starts with run, start, use, do or execute followed by the keyword (run mass ulw research on <link>; in Korean, mass ulw 돌려줘 or 실행해줘) now carries a binding instruction: read the skill before any other tool call, and run mass-ulw as workflow runs. Before, the hint asked the model to decide whether you meant it, and in a real run it skipped mass-ulw and started no workflow. Any other mention, including a prompt that only ends with mass ulw research or asks a question, still gets the hint, and quoted, relayed, negated and delegated mentions never arm it. A single-quoted name ('omo-senpi ultrawork ...') and a relay header naming several recipients ([a -> b + c]) now count as quotes and relays for ulw too, so they no longer arm ultrawork (#10810, #10822).

A session can consult the memory of a project it touches. The first successful read, edit or write under a child project with existing memory lists its note paths and descriptions, without injecting note bodies. Linked projects in a non-git workspace and linked worktrees follow the session's auto_identity mode. Kibitzer ranks up to three recently touched projects separately from the session's own notes, reserves up to half its seats for them, and uses the same persisted search-term cache for each repository. Project notes receive read-only grants; their system/ tree, git metadata, writes and enumeration remain denied. Both memory.project_scope.nudge and .recall default to true and can be disabled separately. (#10044, #10921)

omo.json can say which workspace a session belongs to (#10852). provenance.workspaces lists workspaces by name with optional git_owners and paths; messages between sessions use it to show where the sender works (#10794).

Messages between sessions start with the sender's workspace and project (#10853, #10794). The sender's environment, git owner or configured paths decide it, never the message text; older stored messages say provenance was not recorded (#10794).

A memory git command that hangs past its timeout can now leave evidence behind. With OMO_GIT_TIMEOUT_DIAGNOSTICS_DIR set, a timed-out git records the running process table (and on Windows the stuck git's thread wait states) in that directory before it is stopped; unset, nothing changes. Windows CI uses it to diagnose a rare stalled git add. (#10821, #10914)

Stopping a task no longer risks matching a task with the same id from another task store (#10903). When a task's session shuts down, it finds its own task by the task id in its session context. Task ids are unique only within one task store, so that id is now trusted only when the session's state folder is exactly this store's folder for that task; otherwise the session falls back to matching by its session id. (#10881)

Anonymous usage stats now count each person once. The anonymous id is kept once per user instead of per agent directory, so runs that use their own agent directory, and the CLI next to OmO Desktop, no longer show up as separate people; runs in CI, under a test runner, or with a temporary home directory send nothing by default (OMO_TELEMETRY_ALLOW_AUTOMATION=1 opts back in). This also holds on Windows: a temporary home folder there is recognised too, a home folder that cannot be found turns usage stats off rather than on, and a real profile under the users folder is never treated as temporary. On some machines the anonymous id changes once with this update (#10935).

Refused child tasks report startup failure without waiting for slow teardown. Shutdown still waits for pending cleanup (#10988, fixes #10402).

Fixed

  • Memory facts extraction no longer loops until its deadline when a model fills the optional person field on a project fact with an empty placeholder: the placeholder is dropped and the fact is recorded, while a project fact naming a real person is still refused. A model that resends a refused record_fact call unchanged now ends the run with the facts it already recorded, and a parked queue entry no longer holds back that conversation's later entries (#10918). (#10924)

A bug-fix release: Pascal VOC boxes now follow the devkit convention, and a batch of crashes on edge-case inputs is gone.

  • Pascal VOC export and import use the devkit's box indices, so Detectron2 and other readers see the boxes you wrote.
  • Gemini 2.5 and 3.5 masks survive boxes that leave the 0-1000 range instead of failing the whole response.
  • Crop and icon annotators draw on grayscale scenes.
  • Half-precision box centers stay finite instead of turning into inf.
  • JSON sinks, dataset exports and the video reader stop losing data when something goes wrong.

Drop-in upgrade, with one catch: box-only Pascal VOC objects written by earlier versions now load one pixel larger on the right and bottom edges. The migration guide below shows how to fix them.

✨ Spotlights / highlights

Pascal VOC boxes follow the devkit

DetectionDataset.as_pascal_voc and from_pascal_voc now treat <bndbox> indices as 1-based and inclusive, shifting only xmin and ymin by one, which is what Detectron2 and other devkit readers expect. Export also rounds corners to the nearest pixel instead of truncating them, so a YOLO box that from_yolo loads with float noise no longer grows a pixel. Box-only objects written by 0.31.1 and earlier carry an extra +1 in xmax and ymax; objects exported from masks already used the devkit maxima. (#2748, #2780)

# `dataset` holds one box [10, 20, 40, 60]
dataset.as_pascal_voc(
    images_directory_path="images", annotations_directory_path="annotations"
)
# <bndbox>: xmin=11 ymin=21 xmax=40 ymax=60  (0.31.1: xmax=41 ymax=61)
# a YOLO box loaded as [0, 0, 37.0000001, 29.0000001]: 1 1 37 29  (0.31.1: 1 1 38 30)

Gemini masks survive boxes outside the 0-1000 range

Detections.from_vlm with VLM.GOOGLE_GEMINI_2_5 or VLM.GOOGLE_GEMINI_3_5 raised ValueError as soon as a box_2d coordinate went above 1000 or below 0, even by one, and you lost every detection in the response. The mask is now cropped to the part of its box inside the image, a box wholly outside gets an all-false mask, and boxes inside the image produce the same masks as before. (#2793)

import supervision as sv

# one item: {"box_2d": [500, 500, 1001, 1001], "label": "cat", "mask": "data:image/png;base64,..."}
detections = sv.Detections.from_vlm(
    sv.VLM.GOOGLE_GEMINI_3_5, result, resolution_wh=(1000, 800)
)
detections.mask.shape, int(detections.mask.sum())
# ((1, 800, 1000), 200000)
# 0.31.1: ValueError: could not broadcast input array from shape (400,501) into shape (400,500)

Crop and icon annotators on grayscale scenes

CropAnnotator and IconAnnotator used to raise IndexError or ValueError on scenes shaped (H, W) or (H, W, 1), or given as a Pillow "L" image. Crops now keep the scene's channel layout, and icons are drawn as their gray luminance, blended by their alpha channel. (#2788)

import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

scene = np.zeros((100, 100), dtype=np.uint8)
scene[20:60, 20:60] = 200
detections = sv.Detections(
    xyxy=np.array([[20, 20, 60, 60]], dtype=float), class_id=np.array([0])
)
sv.CropAnnotator().annotate(scene.copy(), detections).shape
# (100, 100)  (0.31.1: IndexError: tuple index out of range)

Half-precision boxes that stay finite

sv.scale_boxes and Detections.get_anchors_coordinates now compute box centers without overflowing float16: a box from 40000 to 60000 used to report an inf center. DetectionsSmoother also compares oriented-box corner distances in float64, which stops float16 and narrow integer coordinates from overflowing; integer coordinates beyond 2**53 still lose low-order pixels in the float64 average. (#2787, #2785)

import numpy as np
import supervision as sv

detections = sv.Detections(
    xyxy=np.array([[40000, 40000, 60000, 60000]], dtype=np.float16)
)
detections.get_anchors_coordinates(sv.Position.CENTER).tolist()
# [[49984.0, 49984.0]]  (0.31.1: [[inf, inf]])

🔄 Migration guide

One behavior change needs your attention: the Pascal VOC box convention. No public symbol was added, renamed or removed in this release, and nothing is deprecated.

Pascal VOC <bndbox> indices affects sv.DetectionDataset.as_pascal_voc and sv.DetectionDataset.from_pascal_voc. Before 0.31.2, export added 1 to all four corners of a box-only object and truncated, and import subtracted 1 from all four. From 0.31.2, both follow the devkit's 1-based, inclusive indices: only xmin and ymin are shifted by one, and export rounds to the nearest pixel. Export rounds every corner to a whole pixel and the loader returns float32 coordinates, so check precision-sensitive boxes after a round trip. Files from different versions don't round-trip. (#2748, #2780)

Box [10, 20, 40, 60] Written <bndbox> Read back by 0.31.2
written by 0.31.1 xmin=11 ymin=21 xmax=41 ymax=61 [10, 20, 41, 61]
written by 0.31.2 xmin=11 ymin=21 xmax=40 ymax=60 [10, 20, 40, 60]
  • Box-only objects (no <polygon>) in files written by 0.31.1 or earlier now load one pixel larger on the right and bottom edges. To restore the original boxes, subtract 1 from <xmax> and <ymax> of those objects only, or re-export the dataset from its source with 0.31.2. Objects exported from masks, which carry a <polygon>, already used the devkit maxima, so leave their files alone: their masks load as before, while their boxes now end one pixel further right and down.
  • Files exported by 0.31.2 match what Detectron2 and other devkit readers expect, so workarounds for the old extra +1 in xmax and ymax can go.

📝 Notable changes

⚠️ Breaking Changes

  • Pascal VOC box extents — as_pascal_voc and from_pascal_voc follow the devkit's 1-based, inclusive <bndbox> indices and export rounds corners to the nearest pixel. Box-only objects written by earlier versions load one pixel larger on the right and bottom edges, so check the migration guide before reading old VOC datasets. (#2748, #2780)

🔧 Fixed

Datasets and file I/O

  • Dataset exports finished without an error even when an image could not be written, leaving image files missing; detection dataset exports and ClassificationDataset.as_folder_structure now raise OSError with the destination path. (#2772)
  • JSONSink.write_and_close() raised ValueError: I/O operation on closed file. when called inside a with block, because the block's exit calls it again; it's now a no-op once the file is closed, like CSVSink.close(). (#2771)
  • JSONSink.append kept references to its input, so reusing NumPy buffers or editing nested metadata changed rows that were already appended; it now snapshots the data. (#2781)
  • NumPy boolean scalars are now written as JSON booleans in JSON files. (#2783)

Detections and VLM

  • Detections.from_vlm with the Gemini 2.5 and 3.5 connectors failed on any item whose box_2d left the 0-1000 range; its mask is now cropped to the image. (#2793)
  • Detections.select() raised an indexing error on selected rows that share a scalar value in data; scalar NumPy values are now preserved. (#2769)
  • sv.mask_iou_batch now treats CompactMask inputs like dense masks: mismatched image shapes raise ValueError, unsupported overlap metrics are rejected even when bounding-box pre-filtering finds no pair, and exact NMS thresholds make the same decision for both. (#2767)
  • sv.scale_boxes and Detections.get_anchors_coordinates overflowed to inf for float16 boxes with large coordinates. (#2787)
  • DetectionsSmoother could overflow or tie on float16 and large integer coordinates when aligning oriented-box corners; integer coordinates beyond 2**53 still lose low-order pixels in the float64 average. (#2785)

Annotators and video

  • CropAnnotator and IconAnnotator raised IndexError or ValueError on grayscale scenes. (#2788)
  • get_video_frames_generator left its video capture open when range validation or the initial seek failed; it now releases the capture and logs any secondary release error without replacing the original error. (#2782)

🏆 Contributors

Welcome to our first-time contributors: 卢文彬, SHLOK SINGH, zurrll, Huashuo Lei, moyunliuyin, Wentao Tong and LEE, WEI-HONG!

  • Avanish Garg (@avanish-garg) — kept Gemini 2.5 and 3.5 masks when a box leaves the 0-1000 range.
  • Mohammad Hijjawi (@MohammadHijjawi97) — made CropAnnotator and IconAnnotator work on grayscale scenes.
  • 卢文彬 (@lu123bing) — fixed inf box centers for half-precision boxes.
  • A Aswanth Raj (@aswanth-07) — fixed overflow in DetectionsSmoother corner alignment.
  • Kaushik Reddy Lingireddy (@Lingikaushikreddy) — rounded Pascal VOC corners instead of truncating them.
  • moyunliuyin (@moyunliuyin) — aligned Pascal VOC export and import with the devkit's box extents.
  • Junghwan (@shaun0927) — fixed JSONSink.append buffer reuse and released video captures when setup fails.
  • Huashuo Lei (@wpyaoxueros) — fixed Detections.select() with scalar data.
  • Wentao Tong (@tongwentao) — made dataset exports raise when an image cannot be written.
  • kevin (@kevin9327) — fixed JSONSink.write_and_close() after the file is closed.
  • Devulapalli Naga Sri Vaishnavi (@Vaishnavi220506) — aligned CompactMask IoU with the dense-mask contract.
  • @zurrll — saved NumPy booleans as JSON booleans.
  • SHLOK SINGH (@buildwithshlok) — added type checking to the annotators tests.
  • LEE, WEI-HONG (@AuricTW) — added a cross_product doctest.
  • Jirka Borovec (@Borda) — prepared the release.

Automated contributions: Dependabot, Copilot, Claude, pre-commit.ci

v2026.9.34openclaw 2026.9.34 Stable2026-10-24T11:38:56Z

This is a gateway-only extended-stable release, which is our current equivalent to LTS. This release is OpenClaw from the end of September 2026, plus critical security updates, reliability and performance fixes, and features like new model support. The latest version of OpenClaw at the time of this release is 2026.10.6

2026.9.34

Highlights

  • Safer agent file edits: apply_patch now validates an ordered envelope before mutating the workspace, so a later invalid hunk cannot delete files changed by an earlier operation. (#160409) Thanks @masatohoshino, @obviyus, and @RomneyDa.
  • More reliable managed upgrades: app-owned updates now converge official plugins alongside core and retain repair diagnostics. Fixes #174120. (#174257) Thanks @kazuyuki-eguchi and @RomneyDa.
  • Memory Wiki data safety: OKF concept re-imports now preserve human-authored notes. Fixes #175700. (#175707) Thanks @YangManBOBO and @RomneyDa.
  • Reliable model startup and selection: Gateway startup now survives model-refresh ownership replacement, and catalog readiness honors the effective primary model's configured account pin. Fixes #178502. (#173366, #178522) Thanks @ericcaiwx-star, @eduardonunesfreire-rgb, and @RomneyDa.
  • Gateway and integration stability: log rotation no longer spins on a deleted /tmp, Buzz relay closure no longer exits the Gateway during authentication, and OpenRouter onboarding accepts valid credentials. Fixes #147269. (#160433, #170591, #173292) Thanks @masatohoshino, @jarvis-modern-mail, @chandraveshchaudhari, @RomneyDa, and @WadeOwenWatts.
  • Plugin hooks restored: before_tool_call hooks now run under openclaw agent exec. Fixes #158824. (#159333) Thanks @joseairosa and @RomneyDa.

Changes

  • Managed update convergence: official plugins are reconciled to the app-managed core version during upgrades, with diagnostics retained for repair paths. Fixes #174120. (#174257) Thanks @kazuyuki-eguchi and @RomneyDa.

Fixes

  • Agent patch atomicity: preflight ordered apply_patch envelopes before mutation so later invalid hunks cannot destroy earlier files. (#160409) Thanks @masatohoshino, @obviyus, and @RomneyDa.
  • Memory Wiki note preservation: retain human-authored notes when OKF concepts are imported again. Fixes #175700. (#175707) Thanks @YangManBOBO and @RomneyDa.
  • Model lifecycle and auth selection: keep startup alive through model-refresh replacement and honor the configured primary account pin during catalog readiness. Fixes #178502. (#173366, #178522) Thanks @ericcaiwx-star, @eduardonunesfreire-rgb, and @RomneyDa.
  • Gateway logging and Buzz stability: avoid deleted-log-target CPU spin and prevent NIP-42 relay closure from exiting the Gateway. Fixes #147269. (#160433, #170591) Thanks @masatohoshino, @jarvis-modern-mail, @RomneyDa, and @WadeOwenWatts.
  • OpenRouter onboarding: accept valid API keys during route verification. (#173292) Thanks @chandraveshchaudhari and @RomneyDa.
  • Agent plugin hooks: restore before_tool_call execution for openclaw agent exec. Fixes #158824. (#159333) Thanks @joseairosa and @RomneyDa.
  • Cross-release updater compatibility: retain the 2026.10.1 launchd observation and updater runtime exports during extended-stable replacement, and conservatively refuse immutable-install mutation on this older release line. (#160663) Thanks @RomneyDa.
  • Patched Node runtime floors: require Node >=24.22.1 <25 || >=26.12.1 across install, update, Docker images, and the macOS app runtime check, so upgrades refuse vulnerable runtimes with a clear next step. (#181073) Thanks @RomneyDa.
  • Dependency advisories: patch zod (GHSA-mrhx-c7xc-m3w5), body-parser, and other production advisories on this release line. (#181341) Thanks @RomneyDa.
  • Session durability: skip empty transcript archive materialization and fence the first creation during transcript reconciliation. (#170122) Thanks @RomneyDa.
  • Claude CLI session continuity: subagent completions no longer reset the Claude CLI session and lose prior context. (#178955) Thanks @Marvinthebored and @RomneyDa.
  • Update recovery: complete interrupted update recovery safely and preserve admission interruption reasons for Doctor follow-up. (#181503, #181870) Thanks @RomneyDa.
  • Backup, Linux, and macOS repairs: carry backup and platform service repairs needed by this release line, including the legacy macOS Gateway status path. (#181466) Thanks @RomneyDa.
  • Release validation compatibility: reconcile branch-native update admission, declaration surfaces, safety baselines, and test fixtures required by the current full-release validation toolchain. (#180988) Thanks @RomneyDa.

Complete contribution record

The expanded maintenance audit covers all 743 selected source rows from the 2026.10 stable and beta release lines after v2026.9.33: 596 unique numbered PRs and 105 unnumbered release companions. The final source-row dispositions are 142 applied, 82 branch-adapted, 128 already covered, and 391 explicitly excluded.

The complete deduplicated PR inventory, mixed source-row sequences, unnumbered companions, and exclusion reasons are preserved in the 2026.9.34 extended-stable backport audit. The grouped notes above remain the user-impact summary rather than repeating the hundreds-row audit.

heygen-com/hyperframes ↗ 4 releases · 4 stable
v0.8.192 Stable2026-10-24T10:50:16Z

HyperFrames v0.8.192

Released on 2026-10-24.

H265 and HDR renders work again on machines with more than 16 cores. Cloud renders of long, cut-heavy edits spend far less time probing and reading audio.

Fixes

  • Engine: H265 renders no longer fail on hosts with more than 16 cores (53e1dfce9e6a, #6193).
  • CLI: A check that hits its deadline keeps the findings it already made (ebb057fb62f1, #6190).
  • CLI: Normalize muted targets before applying tolerance (0b8f5ec8f5ae, #5291).
  • Core: Release decoded preview audio once no clip uses its source (09d7f1c64660, #6178).
  • Studio Server: Project history no longer copies video, audio or huge files (5ebbc8ef6dbf, #6171).
  • CLI: Audit clipped text beneath transparent composition hosts (2a9b9f4e7c2f, #5400).
  • CLI: Refuse undo when a target or backup is missing (9ab4de459988, #5365).
  • Lint: Check timeline registration before explicit font loads (191caf943ab5, #5363).
  • Studio Server: Decode authored audio attributes for loudness (0aa728b1aa24, #5289).
  • CLI: Stage temporary HTML comparisons without recursive copies (bd0be1bdae15, #5286).
  • Core: Preserve blocked addresses in mounted import maps (ecf5db7070c4, #5277).
  • Lint: Read actual font CSS declarations (a1b23f1e4dd2, #5221).
  • CLI: Fail benchmarks with no completed renders (9e533f0887cd, #5303).
  • CLI: Read info metadata from the root composition (8a84bedd38b2, #5299).
  • CLI: Capture images declared only through srcset (1001a7941983, #5298).
  • Parsers: Recognize spaced slideshow type attributes (0a37f9b9bb34, #5326).
  • CLI: Close asset streams when clients disconnect (410030a7331b, #5321).
  • CLI: Preserve portrait orientation during background removal (58752b5cf3e2, #5313).
  • CLI: Tolerate invalid optional package cache manifests (1e6a2f0ff92f, #5349).
  • CLI: Honor HTML attribute casing in frame-rate defaults (c00a1bc1d427, #5348).
  • Core: Preserve literal percent in beat source paths (234b87a4bbbd, #5327).
  • CLI: Preserve stylesheet order during website capture (ad06c60c7402, #5311).
  • CLI: Detect beats from child media sources (e10155ce35b1, #5310).
  • CLI: Retain metadata when Lottie previews exceed the size limit (58578fc22974, #5307).
  • CLI: Show complete history diffs for large text changes (ac6c682a0d77, #5305).
  • Engine: Preserve Windows RSS samples after a query failure (ba5dde78de2e, #5357).
  • Engine: Recognize spaced closing template tags (cad57bf2aa46, #5353).
  • Engine: Retain fresh frames when replacing an empty cache (6fccefe9761b, #5351).
  • CLI: Tolerate removed files during desktop catch-up (e7f6c12b9166, #5350).
  • CLI: Respect image orientation in capture contact sheets (e0317a23c09a, #5295).
  • CLI: Protect batch input from generated manifest (d94a9d7aabb3, #5294).
  • CLI: Init never touches installed skills and no command removes one (0d104e6fca49, #6168).
  • Studio: Preserve caption text when parsing transcripts (886e8696dfc4, #3896).

Performance

  • Producer: The audio task finds sound with a probe and reads URL clips in parallel (acb47de7d298, #6174).
  • Engine: A site's remote files are probed once per render, not once per clip (da3e9b6385ef, #6172).

Docs & Examples

  • Clarify Claude Code plugin auto-update steps (fa5dbd12c969, #5120).

Internal

  • Engine: The GPU probe tests do not start a Chrome from the host cache (3ef28e26c6f4, #6187).
  • Core: Isolate local font fallback from system discovery (14c9eb448751, #5360).
  • Use supported FFmpeg flags for VFR fixtures (bd4d8c6cb5bc, #5352).

A deleted layer that a script still looks up now stays hidden instead of coming back, and a script that throws no longer blocks a render. Preview loads only the clips due next, so it holds up on slow links.

Features

  • Engine: Redraw a small drawElement frame before failing the serial capture (c478110be, #5748).
  • Core: Preview fetches only the clips due next, and drops passed clips still downloading (179098936, #6160).
  • Core: A hidden child of a mover stays out of the blur trail (e077d9dc7, #6155).
  • Sdk: A kept delete drops its media sources and a hidden video is not waited for (44100a537, #6163).
  • Studio: Audio clips in the timeline share the video clip corner radius (579f73bf2, #6159).
  • CLI: Snapshot waits for the image layers a seek reveals before capturing (1552f52fb, #6161).
  • Engine: A composition whose script throws is skipped with a warning, not refused (8df9b6dd3, #6156).
  • Sdk: A stored delete a script still looks up is hidden when overrides replay, not removed (dad825945, #6143).

Performance

Docs & Examples

  • Skills: Remove duplicated sections in skill references (d5526bd48, #6164).

Internal

  • Engine: Only h264 is held to identical bytes across host sizes (19cc96e3f, #6167).

HyperFrames v0.8.190

Released on 2026-10-23.

Motion blur now picks a cheaper way to draw when it can, and renders use less memory. Studio gains a preview seek bar, and an idle editor stops waking the GPU.

Features

  • Automatic tier, 240°/32 defaults, check finding, and Studio stops opting out (79b57ab12, #6108).
  • Core: Capture blur falls back to per-element filters where capture cannot run (4ed781338, #6107).
  • Studio: Add a preview seek bar (2512642d0, #6103).

Fixes

  • Engine: The BeginFrame start-up check waits for the first frame up to its deadline (73718a251, #6149).
  • Engine: A render no longer decodes the videos it replaces with extracted frames (01a523bcf, #6142).
  • CLI: Render -c takes an absolute entry inside the project, relative to the project (9fe0511c2, #6141).
  • Engine: The video frame cache budget is shared by the capture workers (f8ae1483c, #6135).
  • Studio: The thumbnail capture page loads media near the playhead like the preview (28ac4d76b, #6146).
  • Engine: A long audio mix prepares its clips a few at a time (1dc97921c, #6132).

Performance

  • Studio: An idle editor stops waking the GPU four times a second (6ad7c82d2, #6109).
  • AWS Lambda: Warm the audio function while the plan runs (fb2f7c1a8, #6148).

oomol-lab/open-connector ↗ 1 release · 1 stable
v1.9.3 Stable2026-10-24T07:30:29Z

Highlights

  • Embedded runtimes can coexist in one process with independent network policies, including background maintenance and provider requests.
  • Add SQLite/PostgreSQL schema equivalence checks, sharded CI tests, and a web production-build check.
  • Consolidate provider error factories and timeout defaults, extract credential resolution, and add a provider scaffold with safe failure cleanup.
  • Include Slack callback verification, the AllRatesToday provider, Gmail rate-limit recovery, and OAuth refusal-page improvements.

Default behavior change: lazy catalog schemas

The standalone server now loads action schemas on demand by default, matching the embedded runtime. Action metadata stays in memory; schemas are read from catalog files when needed. This reduces startup work and resident memory without changing API response content.

The first access to an uncached provider schema performs a file read, so keep the catalog files available throughout the runtime's lifetime. To restore the previous eager-loading behavior, set OOMOL_CONNECT_CATALOG_LAZY_SCHEMAS=false; embedded hosts can use lazySchemas: false.

What's Changed

  • feat(slackbot): add inbound event verification endpoint by @LM20230311 in https://github.com/oomol-lab/open-connector/pull/774
  • fix(providers): report upstream rate limits as rate_limited by @Tong-bit-art in https://github.com/oomol-lab/open-connector/pull/775
  • feat(providers): add AllRatesToday provider by @cahthuranag in https://github.com/oomol-lab/open-connector/pull/776
  • feat(slackbot): verify interaction callbacks by @LM20230311 in https://github.com/oomol-lab/open-connector/pull/777
  • fix(oauth): show a page for a provider refusal on a runtime authorization by @powerfulZ in https://github.com/oomol-lab/open-connector/pull/778
  • fix(gmail): retry rate-limited hydration instead of failing the page by @powerfulZ in https://github.com/oomol-lab/open-connector/pull/779
  • refactor: isolate runtime egress and strengthen CI safeguards by @l1shen in https://github.com/oomol-lab/open-connector/pull/780

New Contributors

  • @cahthuranag made their first contribution in https://github.com/oomol-lab/open-connector/pull/776
