stablyai/orca ↗ 2 releases · 2 stable
v1.4.239 Stable2026-10-24T07:10:02Z

Two releases today! Check out the v1.4.238 release notes too. That release brought shared unsaved edits across workspaces, richer agent chats and remote account setup, a more capable browser, and smoother phone controls.

Your workspace, working together 🐳

Set up agent skills in one click, keep browser sessions separate between projects, and move more easily between chat and terminal. This release also strengthens the essentials: shared files stay in sync, SSH sessions recover more reliably, and phone interactions feel more predictable.

The short version

  • Skills, ready wherever you work: Install Orca’s skills in one click from setup screens, and install or update them on paired servers and SSH hosts with Orca’s own installer.
  • A browser that fits your projects: Choose shared, per-repo or per-workspace profiles for new tabs. Keep local app logins separate, use a familiar page context menu, and get clearer explanations when a page cannot load.
  • More fluid agent conversations: Split into a fresh chat beside your current one, continue with a terminal agent from the pane header, and keep queued messages and multiple image attachments intact.
  • Safer edits, quieter background work: Shared file views stay current after undo and discard. Non-UTF-8 files ask before conversion, file watching recovers after slowdowns, and Orca watches fewer unrelated files.
  • Remote work with a way back: Recover supported managed SSH servers from a stale lock in Settings, restore terminals after password sign-in, and keep a paired server’s SSH access link through restarts.
  • Better from your phone: Tapping a notification opens the agent that sent it, agent chat tabs can start dictation, terminal copy commands reach the phone clipboard, and Android scrolling keeps the keyboard out of the way.
  • Everyday polish, across languages: Better Korean input, Bengali and other Indic terminal rendering, more complete translations, Jira user pickers, and PR comment links that jump straight to the editor.

Phone updates: Updating Orca on the computer serving your phone updates the served interface. Native download, progress and navigation improvements require an updated native phone app.

Compatibility & upgrade notes

  • Browser profiles: Choose Settings → Browser → Profile for new tabs. Shared remains the default; per-repo and per-workspace profiles apply to new tabs. Paired-server pages use the server’s own profiles.
  • Native chat (experimental): Update paired and SSH hosts alongside Orca for the latest chat and launch fixes. Chat availability now checks the chat runtime separately from the terminal CLI, including supported Antigravity setups.
  • SSH recovery: Recover server… is available for supported managed Linux SSH hosts reporting a stale-lock refusal. It checks the lock and asks you to confirm that no other machine sharing that home is running Orca before clearing it. Phones point you to desktop Settings.
  • Experimental groundwork: Connector work remains behind the off-by-default experimentalConnectors flag. The layout-owner groundwork remains disabled. The empty-group launch actions and child-workspace status toggle were reverted before release.

Product experience

Agents, skills & setup

Get agent skills onto the machines where you work, with clearer launch choices and startup feedback.

v1.4.238 Stable2026-10-23T21:47:22Z

More connected work, safer edits 🐳

This release makes it easier to move between agents, files, browsers and remote machines. Tabs of the same file now share unsaved edits, native chats pick up turns made elsewhere, and the phone gets more dependable terminal gestures and richer tab controls.

The short version

  • Your edits stay together: Tabs of the same file share unsaved text across workspaces. Conflict review sees that live text, workspace deletion lists unsaved files, and stale Markdown or notebook edits no longer overwrite newer work.
  • Chats that keep up: Codex and Pi show turns made outside the chat. Long pastes can become text attachments, Codex questions get answer cards, and OMP gains image sending and actionable plan-review cards.
  • More control over agents: Pick chat or terminal when creating a workspace, set that choice for your default agent, add Claude and Codex accounts on supported remote servers, and install shared skills for 11 more agents.
  • A more capable browser: A workspace-aware new tab, address-bar suggestions, remembered site permissions, per-site appearance and zoom, and page-loading progress on desktop and phone.
  • A smoother phone experience: See agent activity in tabs, rename with a double-tap, scroll back through earlier chat messages, select terminal text more naturally, and return to your terminal reading position after resuming.
  • Better visibility and recovery: Inspect local terminals in Resource Manager, use plain SSH when a host’s move to an Orca server is blocked, and keep pairings through managed-server updates and recovery.
  • Everyday polish: Brazilian Portuguese, language selection during onboarding, searchable release builds, clearer history-scan progress, and Resolve with AI for paused merges, rebases and cherry-picks—even after file conflicts are fixed.

Phone updates: Updating Orca on the computer serving your phone updates the served interface. The new Home → New Workspace entry and native iOS dictation fixes require an updated native phone app; the home-screen entry ships with the next app build.

Compatibility & upgrade notes

  • Remote accounts: Update the paired server for the new Claude and Codex Add Account flow. Windows servers and older hosts retain the orca account add guidance. Credentials stay on the server; remote re-authentication of an existing account is outside this change.
  • Native chat (experimental): Update paired and SSH hosts alongside Orca for the latest chat fixes. Agent version checks now accept newer releases and prereleases that meet the required minimum; a known older version shows update guidance.
  • Resource Manager: The new PTYs view covers local terminals. Ending a terminal requires host support for verifying the selected session; older hosts refuse unchecked termination.
  • HTML files: Opening HTML in preview by default was reverted for this release.
  • Experimental groundwork: Layout-owner and sidebar changes listed below remain disabled. Connector configuration is off by default, and the new optional agent-write controls have no existing callers enabled.

nightlyNvim development (prerelease) build Prerelease2026-10-24T05:22:42Z 
NVIM v0.13.0-dev-1944+g7b87ce822e
Build type: RelWithDebInfo
LuaJIT 2.1.1792527110

Release notes

  • Changelog (fixes + features)
  • News (:help news in Nvim)

Install

Windows

Zip

  1. Download nvim-win64.zip (or nvim-win-arm64.zip for ARM)
  2. Extract the zip
  3. Run nvim.exe in your terminal

MSI

  1. Download nvim-win64.msi (or nvim-win-arm64.msi for ARM)
  2. Run the MSI
  3. Run nvim.exe in your terminal

Note: On Windows "Server" you may need to install vcruntime*.dll.

macOS (x86_64)

  1. Download nvim-macos-x86_64.tar.gz
  2. Run xattr -c ./nvim-macos-x86_64.tar.gz (to avoid "unknown developer" warning)
  3. Extract: tar xzvf nvim-macos-x86_64.tar.gz
  4. Run ./nvim-macos-x86_64/bin/nvim

macOS (arm64)

  1. Download nvim-macos-arm64.tar.gz
  2. Run xattr -c ./nvim-macos-arm64.tar.gz (to avoid "unknown developer" warning)
  3. Extract: tar xzvf nvim-macos-arm64.tar.gz
  4. Run ./nvim-macos-arm64/bin/nvim

Linux (x86_64)

If your system does not have the required glibc version, try the (unsupported) builds for older glibc.

AppImage

  1. Download nvim-linux-x86_64.appimage
  2. Run chmod u+x nvim-linux-x86_64.appimage && ./nvim-linux-x86_64.appimage
    • If your system does not have FUSE you can extract the appimage:
      ./nvim-linux-x86_64.appimage --appimage-extract
./squashfs-root/usr/bin/nvim

Tarball

  1. Download nvim-linux-x86_64.tar.gz
  2. Extract: tar xzvf nvim-linux-x86_64.tar.gz
  3. Run ./nvim-linux-x86_64/bin/nvim

Linux (arm64)

AppImage

  1. Download nvim-linux-arm64.appimage
  2. Run chmod u+x nvim-linux-arm64.appimage && ./nvim-linux-arm64.appimage
    • If your system does not have FUSE you can extract the appimage:
      ./nvim-linux-arm64.appimage --appimage-extract
./squashfs-root/usr/bin/nvim

Tarball

  1. Download nvim-linux-arm64.tar.gz
  2. Extract: tar xzvf nvim-linux-arm64.tar.gz
  3. Run ./nvim-linux-arm64/bin/nvim

Other

  • Install by package manager

oh-my-codex v0.21.35

0.21.35 is a patch release that fixes legacy recovery journal ownership and platform-aware replay logic.

This release addresses issues introduced in v0.21.34's shutdown preservation (#3896) where legacy recovery journals from other workers could block a healthy worker's shutdown. The fix scopes journal recovery to the owning worktree and enforces platform-aware naming conventions, preventing parent traversal attempts and ensuring module-only replay.

Highlights

  • RESILIENCE: Worktree-scoped journal recovery (#3903): A pending legacy (array-format) recovery journal owned by another worker no longer blocks a healthy worker's shutdown with shutdown_worktree_preservation_failed. This fixes a regression introduced by v0.21.34's shutdown preservation (#3896).
  • SAFETY: Platform-aware legacy journal ownership (#3904): Legacy journal names beginning with ".." are no longer treated as parent traversal attempts. Platform-aware ownership checking prevents cross-worker journal contamination.
  • MODULE ISOLATION: Modules-only replay (#3904): Legacy journal replay is now enforced to operate only on modules, preventing accidental state corruption from misconfigured legacy journals.

Compatibility

  • No breaking API changes; recovery robustness improvements only.
  • Team runtime users: If you experienced recovery journal blocking on shutdown in v0.21.34, this release resolves the issue.
  • Existing sessions with pending legacy recovery journals will be handled correctly by the platform-aware logic.
  • The fix improves legacy recovery robustness without changing the recovery API contract.

Known issues

  • #3898 (live-pin fix) is in progress (#3900); Codex 0.164.0 hook validation was invalidated by .omx-live-pin files in the plugin cache. Workaround: manually clear .omx-live-pin from the cache if running Codex 0.164.0.

Validation

  • Pinned candidate c6a41e75a04a77c7507b5987246abad80029ac9a passed CI run at 02:17Z on 2026-10-24: 17 checks succeeded, 8 conditional checks skipped, no failures.
  • Both macOS Ralplan preflight security jobs PASSED (not cancelled or failed).
  • All local gates pass: build, typecheck, lint, and team runtime legacy recovery tests.
  • All code review findings addressed.
  • Ready for merge and release.

v0.21.34 Stable2026-10-23T23:41:54Z

oh-my-codex v0.21.34

0.21.34 is a patch release that preserves worker worktrees when shutdown cannot save work (PR #3896).

This release fixes an issue where worker worktrees could be deleted during shutdown even when checkpointing or merging failed, or when the working directory contained ignored files. The shutdown process no longer deletes worker worktrees in these failure cases, allowing recovery state to be preserved for retries. Submodules, report provenance, and partial pane/prompt teardown are still handled correctly.

Highlights

  • PRESERVATION: Worker worktrees survive shutdown failure (#3896): When shutdown could not save work (checkpointing failure, merge failure, or ignored files present), the process would still delete worker worktrees, losing recovery state. The fix preserves worktrees in these cases, allowing retries with full state intact. This also resolves issue #3897.
  • Recovery state retention: Shutdown failures no longer erase the work that was being preserved; recovery can be attempted on the next run.
  • Selective teardown (#3896): Submodules, report provenance, and partial pane/prompt cleanup proceed independently; a failure in one component no longer cascades to worktree deletion.

Compatibility

  • No breaking API changes; shutdown resilience improvement only.
  • Team runtime users: If shutdown failed to save work in earlier versions, worker worktrees were lost. Upgrade to v0.21.34 to preserve recovery state in shutdown failure cases.
  • Existing sessions remain unaffected unless they experienced shutdown failures with ignored files or checkpointing errors.
  • The fix improves robustness without changing the shutdown API contract.

Known issues

  • #3898 (live-pin fix) is in progress (#3900); Codex 0.164.0 hook validation was invalidated by .omx-live-pin files in the plugin cache. Workaround: manually clear .omx-live-pin from the cache if running Codex 0.164.0.

Validation

  • Pinned candidate bc7efc1c1c504b84a28cd4b24c1f3d6af08e6217 passed CI run at 20:16Z on 2026-10-24: 17 checks succeeded, 8 conditional checks skipped, no failures.
  • Both macOS Ralplan preflight security jobs PASSED (not cancelled or failed).
  • All local gates pass: build, typecheck, lint, and team runtime shutdown preservation tests.
  • All code review findings addressed.
  • Ready for merge and release.

New

Beads v1.3.2

v1.3.2 — the second patch release on the 1.3 line. Released 2026-10-24, cut from hotfix/1.3.1 at 9b65b9e19. It ships exactly the code that was qualified as v1.3.2-rc.3; the only change since that candidate is the version stamp.

There is no schema migration, and the embedded Dolt engine is unchanged (Dolt 2.2.0). Upgrading from v1.3.1 or any v1.3.2 release candidate is a binary swap. If you are coming from v1.3.0 or earlier, read the v1.3.1 release notes first — everything in them applies, and this release adds to it.

This is a fix-only release. It closes two ways v1.3.1's new retention and backup paths could lose data, makes the post-commit blocked-state recheck safe under concurrent writes, lets a least-privilege Dolt user write again, removes an export stall on large wisp sets, and rebuilds with Go 1.26.10 and patched dependencies. It also carries an upgrade note for every store that crossed migration 0059 under bd 1.3.0 or later: read it before you upgrade.

Highlights

  • bd purge no longer deletes the closed root of a chain that still has live work under it (#7041, fixes #7031). v1.3.1's live-dependent protection only covered a closed bead a live bead pointed at directly, so an orchestrator's bd purge --wisps-plane --older-than ... retention sweep could delete a closed root above a closed child above an open grandchild, orphaning both. Protection now propagates up the whole closed chain.
  • Auto-backup never claims a commit the snapshot does not contain (#7044, fixes #7032). The watermark is read before the sync, so a commit that lands mid-sync stays pending for the next backup instead of being skipped as "no changes".
  • The fan-in recheck no longer reverts concurrent writes (#7146, backport of #6876, fixes #7030). On the Dolt server backend, the post-commit blocked-state recheck could write rows other sessions had just committed back to their earlier values. It now runs in its own transaction and publishes its Dolt commit after that transaction commits.
  • A least-privilege Dolt user can write again (#7786, backport of #7322). bd create --graph, bd mol wisp, bd history and bd recompute-blocked no longer fail with command denied for a server user granted EXECUTE on only dolt_add/dolt_commit.
  • bd export --all no longer stalls on workspaces with many wisps (#7603, backport of #6444, with #7785). Bulk readers read at most 200 ids per statement, and a repeated id is read once.
  • Security rebuild. Release binaries build with Go 1.26.10 (#7732), and x/net, x/crypto, grpc and thrift are raised past every fixable advisory that reaches the binary (#6355, #7495).

Upgrading Notes

  • After upgrading from bd 1.3.0 or earlier, run bd recompute-blocked once per workspace (#7037). Migration 0059, first shipped in v1.3.0, recomputes the stored is_blocked flag with a recursive query. On Dolt servers older than 2.4.0, and on the embedded engine, a query-planner bug (dolthub/dolt#11886, fixed in Dolt 2.4.0) drops the query's parent-child edge filter, so blockedness spreads across every dependency type, including relates-to, discovered-from and tracks. Beads that are not blocked are marked blocked and silently disappear from bd ready and bd list --ready. The flag is stored, so the damage persists until it is recomputed, and nothing in v1.3.2 repairs it automatically. This applies to every workspace whose store crossed migration 0059 under bd 1.3.0 or later, which includes a workspace now on v1.3.1 that was first created by 1.2.x or earlier. The command is idempotent, reports rows_corrected, and changes nothing on a workspace that was not affected.
  • bd purge keeps more closed beads (#7041). Every closed bead in a chain above a live bead is now kept and counted in live_dependent_skipped, on every backend. A retention sweep that used to delete such a root no longer does, so its purged count can drop.
  • The bd purge --limit N confirmation suggests a --force command that keeps --limit (#7540, fixes #7534). The suggested command used to drop --limit, so running it as printed deleted every eligible row instead of N. If you copied that suggestion into a script, check it.
  • A negative --older-than that overflows is refused on bd purge and bd prune (#7540, fixes #7524). A large negative day count, such as --older-than=-213503d, used to wrap to a small positive age and purge.
  • bd export fails when it cannot classify wisp-plane rows (#7603). When the wisps table exists but its membership cannot be read, export now fails with failed to classify wisp-plane rows instead of silently exporting without wisp markers. Only a missing wisps table is tolerated.

Fixed

  • bd purge keeps the whole closed chain above a live bead (#7041, fixes #7031). Take a closed root R, a closed child S1 and an open grandchild S2. v1.3.1 protected S1, because S2 is live, but not R, because its only dependent S1 is closed, so purge deleted R and orphaned S1 and S2; --dry-run reported the same deletion. Protection now propagates through closed candidates until nothing changes, on the Dolt server, embedded and proxied backends.
  • The auto-backup watermark no longer runs ahead of the snapshot (#7044, fixes #7032). Auto-backup read Dolt HEAD after the sync and recorded it as the newest commit backed up, so a commit that landed during the sync was recorded as backed up although the snapshot lacked it, and auto-backup then reported "no changes since last backup" until HEAD moved again. Only opted-in auto-backup (backup.enabled: true) was affected; bd backup sync records no commit watermark.
  • The post-commit blocked-state recheck no longer reverts concurrent writes (#7146, backport of #6876, fixes #7030). v1.3.1's #6716 fan-in fix minted its Dolt commit while its own SQL transaction was still open. DOLT_ADD stages the table from the session's BEGIN-time root, so the commit could write issues rows that other sessions had just committed back to their BEGIN-time values. The recheck runs only when unblocking writes (closes, dependency removals, deletes) race, which is exactly when this matters. The recompute now runs alone in its own retried transaction and the Dolt commit is published after it. A failed trailing commit is counted as post_tx_commit_dropped and logged, instead of being reported as a recheck failure, because the flag repair itself is already committed.
  • A least-privilege Dolt user can write again (#7786, backport of #7322). Two fresh-connection paths ran CALL DOLT_CHECKOUT even when the session was already on the requested branch: the fallback for the ignored-tables transaction, and the pinned connection used by long-timeout versioned reads and the blocked recompute. A server user granted EXECUTE on only dolt_add/dolt_commit is denied even that no-op checkout. The checkout now runs only when the session is on a different branch.
  • bd export --all no longer stalls on workspaces with many wisps (#7603, backport of #6444). The bulk label, comment, dependency and issue readers sent every id in one IN (...) list, and Dolt's cost grows faster than linearly in the list length; one reported workspace stopped completing exports past about 21k wisps. The readers now read at most 200 ids per statement, and export reads the wisp-plane relations only for ids that are wisps. A repeated id is read once, so batching never duplicates or drops a row (#7785).
  • bd purge --limit N confirmation and --older-than overflow (#7784, backport of #7540, fixes #7534 and #7524). See Upgrading Notes.

Security

  • Release binaries build with Go 1.26.10 (#7787, backport of #7732), which distrusts the compromised eMudhra intermediate CAs in crypto/x509. release.yml uses uv 0.13.4, which ships the same distrust.
  • Dependency floors raised (#7787): golang.org/x/net v0.60.0 and golang.org/x/crypto v0.57.0 (backport of #6355), and google.golang.org/grpc v1.83.2 and github.com/apache/thrift v0.24.0 (backport of #7495). govulncheck reported 16 reachable advisories on rc.2's module set and none on rc.3's, which is the v1.3.2 module set.

Validation

  • v1.3.2 is the qualified rc.3 code. The tag (9b65b9e19) differs from v1.3.2-rc.3 (0dee73e43) only in the version stamp, the CHANGELOG, the bd info digest, and package and plugin version metadata.
  • Every fix landed on hotfix/1.3.1 as a cherry-pick -x PR of a commit already on main, tested at its head. The backport PRs (#7220, #7146, #7786, #7784, #7603, #7787) and the three RC prep PRs (#7221, #7461, #7788) each passed the full PR matrix of 120–122 checks, including the required CI Gate / Required gate that PRs into hotfix/** now run (#7198, ported in #7217). The promotion PR (#7809) passed 121 checks plus the Nightly Full Tests workflow by dispatch, once for the full test suite (40042534271) and once for the PR Linux command suite (40042536408).
  • The release pipeline completed green (run 40044707863): verify-version-consistency, both goreleaser legs (linux and macOS), both package gates (MCP and npm), publish-pypi, publish-npm and release attestation. The tag-triggered Migration Test Harness (40044708076) and Cross-Version Smoke Tests (40044707912) also passed. 11 assets were published: linux amd64/arm64, darwin amd64/arm64, windows amd64/arm64, freebsd amd64, android arm64, the contract corpus, an SPDX SBOM and checksums. All three release candidates also completed their release pipelines.
  • Qualified against a real downstream consumer before the tag. Gas City's hotfix/1.5.1 branch, pinned to v1.3.2-rc.3, passed its full RC Gate on the first attempt: 40034407401, at 9d970f7cc8. No job failed: the Linux CI parity tiers (including the beads topology acceptance, the bd CLI contract jobs against the current and minimum-supported bd, and a contract radar against beads main), acceptance A, B and C, all integration shards, tutorial goldens 1–6, the four worker-core providers, the goreleaser snapshot, and the full macOS regression set.

Installing

Pre-compiled binaries for Linux, macOS (Intel & Apple Silicon), Windows (AMD64 & ARM64), Android/Termux (ARM64), and FreeBSD are attached to this release.

Homebrew (macOS/Linux):

brew install beads

Quick Install (macOS/Linux/FreeBSD):

curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gastownhall/beads/main/scripts/install.sh | bash

Windows (PowerShell):

irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gastownhall/beads/main/install.ps1 | iex

Manual Install: Download the appropriate binary for your platform below, extract it, and place it in your PATH.

Whichever method you use, run which -a bd afterwards. A second, older bd earlier in PATH is the mixed-version fleet problem described in the v1.3.0 upgrading notes. Then run bd recompute-blocked once per workspace if the first upgrading note applies to you.

Contributors

Thanks to everyone who contributed to v1.3.2 (between v1.3.1 and v1.3.2):

@bee-ghosttrack, @bourgois, @brandonmartin, @julianknutsen, @rjgeng

paperclipai/paperclip ↗ 1 release · 1 stable
v2026.1023.0 Stable2026-10-24T00:03:59Z

Paperclip v2026.1023.0

Released: 2026-10-23

Paperclip v2026.1023.0 carries 200 commits, promoted from 2026.1012.1-beta.0. The headline is private work: a task or project can now be marked private and shared with named people and agents; everyone else cannot open it, find it in task lists or search, read its run transcripts, or reach it through a plugin. Around that: agents can run through your own model gateway (OpenRouter, Amazon Bedrock, Google Gemini, or any OpenAI Responses, Anthropic Messages, or Chat Completions endpoint), Slack bots set themselves up through Slack's Manifest API, the GitHub review bot gets a two-screen setup and a real Paperclip Review status check, Costs becomes an exact ledger that also shows monthly subscription fees, and connected assistants can edit tasks, upload files, and configure agents over MCP. Underneath, OpenAI Dot and Pi 1.0 join the experimental Runner, native OpenCode streams as it types, each agent gets a persistent cryptographic identity, and idle instances stop polling the database every second.

Breaking Changes

  • Operators can now edit the company. The Operator role preset grows from one grant (tasks:assign) to fourteen: agent creation and configuration, skills, environments, invitations, task assignment, pipelines, connections, tool management and use, and audit reads. Existing Operators pick up the missing grants through the normal startup seeding; custom grant scopes are kept. Join approval and member-permission management stay out of the preset, and inviting an Admin now requires join approval while inviting an Owner also requires member-permission management. Review your member roles if Operators were meant to be read-mostly. (#15377)
  • GitHub review bots move behind their own experimental setting. The GitHub Code Review Bot catalog entry, its setup, and its management screens appear only while Settings → Experimental → GitHub review bots (enableGitHubReviewBots, off by default) is on; existing bots keep running while it is off. The old setup-method and delegated-agent screens are gone, and per-person automatic-run flags are replaced by author include/exclude filters (legacy people[].automaticReviews values are read but ignored). (#15416)
  • Budgets hold on unpriced usage by default. Each budget policy gains an unpriced-usage setting that defaults to block: while a run's usage has no reliable price, the policy counts as at its limit until the charge is resolved through the audited cost adjustment flow. Set the policy to allow to keep running on unpriced usage. (#14997)

Highlights

  • Private tasks and projects — Mark a task private when you create it, or make a project private with its own member list; a personal private project is created for you on first use. Private work is readable only by its responsible user, creator, current assignee, named grantees, and private-project members, and that rule applies to task lists and task counts, search, activity, run detail, transcripts, events, and logs, documents, attachments, work products, and every plugin read. Two surfaces stay company-wide on purpose: dashboard and sidebar totals may count private work without exposing a title or identifier, and the company run list shows a locked row for a private task's run with only the agent, status, timing, token, and cost fields, so budget oversight keeps working. Privacy flows down to children; sharing a child never exposes its parent or siblings. Owners and admins do not see private tasks by default and must request ?breakGlass=true, which writes an audit row and a warning notice on the task. Agents' access is intersected with the run's responsible user, so reusing an agent does not carry another person's permissions. (#14717, #10633, #14718)
  • Bring your own model gateway — Connectors gains rows for OpenRouter, Amazon Bedrock, Google Gemini, and generic Responses API, Messages API, Chat Completions API, and local endpoints. URLs, protocol, region, and credentials live on the connection; the agent's Harness / Runtime page picks a compatible Connection from a dropdown and the model picker accepts manual IDs. Codex (legacy and Runner) routes to OpenRouter or custom Responses endpoints, Claude (legacy and Runner) to OpenRouter, custom Messages endpoints, or Bedrock, and OpenCode and Hermes to OpenRouter or custom Chat Completions endpoints. OpenRouter connections without an explicit model list load OpenRouter's public catalog. (#14970, #15341)
  • Slack bots set themselves up — New Slack bot drafts default to automatic setup: paste a temporary App configuration token, Paperclip creates the app through Slack's Manifest API, installs it through OAuth, links your Slack account, uploads the agent's avatar, and verifies delivery in a four-screen wizard with no Slack CLI involved (#15413). A new Require at-mention setting stops thread replies from waking the agent without an explicit mention (#15612); a follow-up sent after a Slack Stop starts a fresh turn instead of stalling (#15737); and Slack agents now know the saved slash command people use to link their accounts, link every task they create, and report results and review requests back in the originating thread (#15576, #15579, #15611).
  • A two-screen GitHub review bot — Setup is now Choose agent, then Connect GitHub under a personal account or organization; GitHub asks for creation and installation consent, and Paperclip stores the App secrets locally, imports repository access, and verifies delivery. Each accepted request gets one editable App-owned progress comment, and review assessments publish a Paperclip Review check for the reviewed commit with a configurable passing score (1–5) that branch protection can require. A self-hosted instance needs one Paperclip Cloud approval before its first managed GitHub connection, because Cloud hosts the fixed OAuth callback and signed webhook inbox; tokens are sealed to your instance. (#15416)
  • Costs you can reconcile — Accounting is now a durable, exact ledger: usage receipts are fsynced and replayed after failures, retries settle one charge, amounts keep decimal cents, and every event is marked reported, estimated, or unpriced instead of silently zero (#14991, #14997). The Costs page reports each connected ChatGPT or Claude subscription's monthly fee once beside API spend, lets you enter the real price, and keeps ambiguous plans unpriced (#15634); quota reads are scoped to authorized company accounts (#14994); cost gaps are listed by agent with links to the affected runs, the model the runtime actually selected is recorded, and a retry appears only when saved evidence is ready (#15948); and historical pricing gaps show as a neutral note under the totals rather than a red error (#15459).
  • Assistants that can do more over MCP — A connected Claude Code, Codex, or other MCP assistant can now edit tasks, finish or block them, write documents and revisions, register deliverables, upload files through expiring tickets, and, with a separately consented configuration scope, manage agent settings and instructions, projects and repositories, and skills (#15380). Connections are named by owner and client ("Dotta's Codex connection") with the authorizing person's avatar, revoked rows disappear, and the copied invitation is shorter (#15411).
  • Sixteen more apps in the catalog — Gauge (#15596), Superagent (#15394), Telem.AI web search (#15379), Enterpret (#13906), Calendly, Exa, Firecrawl, GSC Wizard, Parallel Search, Tavily, and Windsor.ai (#15621), and Bitly, Context7, Hugging Face, and Resend (#15686) join as verified hosted MCP connections. Sentry sign-in discovers OAuth through its MCP resource metadata, so setup no longer asks for a client ID and secret (#15837), and OAuth grants now record whether each scope came from the provider or from Paperclip's request (#14059).
  • New Runner providers — OpenAI Dot joins as a standalone experimental agent choice: pair your Dot with a one-use code, and the Runner delivers assignments over MCP Events while Dot uses its own tools and reports back (#15402, #15414, #15581, #15734). Pi 1.0 runs through the experimental Runner with explicit provider and model selection (#14921), and the Cursor Runner integration is consolidated onto mainline recovery behavior with a public install path (#15075).
  • Codex and OpenCode that just start — Native Codex uses the installed Codex CLI and accepts usable older or newer versions, so a clean npm install no longer needs a global command (#15555); a model that the sandbox's Codex CLI is too old for is swapped for a compatible one with a visible warning instead of failing every turn (#15399, #15519); saved runs survive server upgrades (#15518); and task environment variables reach later turns and tool commands (#15451). Native OpenCode streams text as it arrives (#15708), starts without the postinstall script that package managers skip (#15702), and selects the bundled Linux assets for remote runs without path overrides (#15721).
  • Reports you can open on the task — HTML attachments and workspace .html files render in an opaque-origin sandbox with view-source and download controls (#15447), and CSV files open as tables with row numbers, sticky headers, and record counts (#15445).
  • Clearer task provenance and waits — A follow-up task an agent creates while working on a task now defaults to that task as its parent, and the task page shows "Created from <task> by <agent>" (#15762); native agents can schedule their own one-shot task monitor and yield until it fires (#15446); the monitor card gets an X with a confirmation (#15735); and a saved pull request stays visible in Properties with its review request and a Check status action even when the provider lookup fails (#15375).
  • Your primary agent — Each person gets one primary agent per company, shown with a crown on the roster and used as the fallback for new tasks and Chat when there is no recent choice; the first agent you create becomes primary automatically and can be changed on the agent profile (#15470).
  • Company decision models and fast responses — Company Settings can bind one shared OpenAI or OpenRouter API connection for small typed model decisions, with permission checks, budget reservations, and a Costs → Decisions history (#15473). On top of it, Experimental fast responses posts a short acknowledgement comment within three seconds of a human message while the agent starts its normal run, in tasks, Agent Chat, and Slack and GitHub threads (#15748).

Fixes

  • Workspaces and sandboxes — A transient sandbox copy-back failure is retried up to three times before the task is held for repair, and remaining holds explain what happened in plain language (#15920); a remote sandbox whose required copy-back failed is kept, with its files, behind an explicit repair decision instead of being deleted by cleanup (#15479, #15790); server shutdown waits for a legacy adapter's workspace export before releasing its sandbox lease (#15857); a reused saved worktree keeps its original repository when project settings change (#15528); an accepted native result is no longer mistaken for lost work by the orphan reaper after a restart (#15718); OpenCode runs in the realized workspace via --dir (#11438); Daytona OpenCode sessions keep their deadlines (#15905); and OpenCode timeouts no longer claim the configured deadline expired (#15789).
  • Runs, recovery, and questions — A retry no longer burns itself while a stopped run's environment is still cleaning up, and settled repair instructions stop reappearing in later wakes (#15463); a review wait whose automatic repair also leaves no wake path now records a board decision instead of sitting silently (#15764); a parent is woken again when a child finishes requested revisions (#15372); native runs resume cleanly after connection approval decisions with final usage retained (#15471, #15420, #15514); a pending tool request expires on its own when the user has already connected the service in Apps (#15856); agents stop re-asking questions that moved into feed history (#15392); archiving a task during its completion no longer deadlocks (#15615); and a task policy with a monitor but no stages no longer crashes the task page (#15593).
  • Adapters — Claude CLI sessions resume across per-run agent file copies (#15437); Hermes gets managed instructions through its system overlay instead of a copy in every resumed user turn (#15439); and external agents such as Dot are told to use their own tools when a Paperclip app is missing (#15734).
  • Connections and MCP — One oversized or malformed MCP reply fails only that call instead of locking the whole connection in an error state (#15462); remote MCP callbacks keep an explicitly saved empty agent selection, token exchange sends Accept: application/json, and saved hidden-provider drafts resume from Finish setup (#15686); Airtable, Calendly, and other verified providers get the registration and form fixes found in live testing (#15621); and the sidebar keeps its last plugin items quiet when the server is unreachable (#15588).

Improvements

  • Hiring, approval, pause, resume, and termination run through a durable agent lifecycle with explicit states: proposed hires stay pending until approval, approved hires are prepared and have their harness configuration verified before work, required plugins get callbacks at each step, and the agent page shows lifecycle progress with a retry action (#15631, #15391); plugins can consume a durable resource lifecycle journal with acknowledgments, seeded with a one-time baseline of existing agents and projects, and project archive and restore now write journal events (#15343, #15371).
  • Every agent gets a persistent Ed25519 keypair, created on hire or on its next managed run, encrypted at rest and handed to managed processes as PAPERCLIP_AGENT_KEY_ID, PAPERCLIP_AGENT_PUBLIC_KEY, and PAPERCLIP_AGENT_PRIVATE_KEY; the public key appears on the agent overview (#15352).
  • Agents can file complaints and suggestions about their tooling into the instance's agent_commentary table through new complain and suggestion-box skills or native submit_complaint and submit_suggestion tools, keeping that feedback out of task threads (#15367).
  • Idle instances go quiet: chat delivery, provider action, Slack sync, email, Browser Use cleanup, and five server delivery queues now wake from committed writes and known deadlines instead of scanning the database every second or three (#15625, #15750, #15757, #15802, #15808, #15822); hosts that park idle instances get an idle-sleep safety report that fences accepted work, drains plugin workers, and treats finished logins, consumed retries, and verified delivery history as history rather than pending work (#15522, #15599, #15761, #15851, #15897, #15907), with an opt-in final backup checkpoint before sleep (#15629).
  • Task notifications show the actor's name and avatar and hide your own actions (#15695); other people's comments in task chat appear on the left with their name and avatar, and only yours are on the right in blue (#15494); an agent blocked by an AI connection its responsible user cannot use shows an expanded error naming the agent and connection with a link to its AI settings (#15741); and a teammate without the agent's required personal AI account can connect their own from inside the chat and resume the message (#15376).
  • The task composer keeps its model label steady while the effort slider moves and the slider is larger (#15444), nested selectors scroll with the wheel and touch (#15374), the project picker always offers No project (#15382), routine descriptions keep code-block pastes in the code block and gain a copy control (#15773), confirmation cards stack the prompt above the target pill and hide unlabeled machine keys (#15895), chat connection and recovery cards share one surface (#15771), the Slack chat-or-tools chooser gets icons (#15574), the Workspace filter leaves the task and inbox filter menus (#15788), and the star and leave buttons leave the agent index (#15400).
  • Tasks whose starting branch does not exist in the repository show a branch repair card that offers the remote's default branch or a typed branch and retries through the normal admission gates (#15726); a GitHub reference the instance's credentials cannot see is reported as inaccessible and re-checked instead of frozen as "Not found" (#15906); and the Paperclip skill ships its own issue-update helper and honors a harness checkout instead of demanding a second one (#15554, #15548).
  • Workspace jobs that exit non-zero return 422 workspace_job_failed with the job's own output instead of a 500 (#15941); custom source launchers get the native Runner WebSocket transport from the shared HTTP server constructor (#15682); a refused local Hermes Gateway connection explains which host to check (#15520); and pi-local's unavailable-model error no longer dumps the model catalog (#13628).
  • Failure reports carry bounded evidence for Daytona acquisition timeouts and provider state, workspace base-ref resolution, sandbox transfer and sync-out errors, orphan process loss, ACP bridge terminal frames, Git worktree inspection, and stackless browser rejections (#15946, #15736, #15719, #15637, #15481, #15475, #15478, #15525, #15940), while proven configuration blockers such as a missing user secret, an unchosen AI account, a credential not shared with the responsible user, a local-directory project with a worktree policy, or an external service outage stay out of Sentry (#15472, #15618, #15714, #15521, #15590).

Upgrade Guide

  • Migrations 0306–0333 run on upgrade: 0306 allows google in the AI account-default provider checks; 0307 rewrites the lifecycle-event action constraint; 0308 adds agent_identity_keys; 0309 adds plugin_lifecycle_acknowledgments, indexes the lifecycle journal, and seeds a one-time baseline event per existing agent and project; 0310 adds agent_commentary; 0311 adds MCP attachment upload and file ticket tables; 0312 adds accounting receipt, reservation, adjustment, invoice, and provider snapshot tables, widens cost columns to numeric, and adds the budget unpriced-usage policy (default block); 0313 adds issue_access_grants and project_access_members, adds visibility to tasks and projects (default open), and backfills privacy parent edges and run bindings in 1,000-row batches; 0314 binds historical inline draft images to their first task; 0315 adds user_company_preferences and backfills a primary agent from history; 0316 adds decision model tables; 0317 adds OpenAI Dot binding, mailbox, and assignment tables; 0318 adds chat_slack_registrations; 0319 makes Dot agent refresh tokens non-expiring; 0320 adds agent lifecycle columns and derives lifecycle_state from each agent's current status; 0321 adds chat_endpoints.require_at_mention; 0322 adds AI subscription account and price tables; 0323 adds GitHub registration owner columns; 0324–0330 add the experimental voice session tables; 0331 adds fast-response tables and issue_comments.origin; 0332 adds a question-history index concurrently; 0333 adds cost data-quality indexes. 0313 and 0314 run outside a single transaction and commit each batch, so an interrupted upgrade leaves them pending and safe to rerun; expect them to take longer on instances with large run histories.
  • New environment variables, none required: PAPERCLIP_ISSUE_PRIVACY_MODE (default enforce; shadow logs would-deny decisions without enforcing, off disables the predicate) (#10633); PAPERCLIP_DB_BACKUP_IDLE_CHECKPOINT_ENABLED=1 opts an instance with automatic backups into taking a final verified backup before idle sleep (off by default) (#15629); PAPERCLIP_RESPONSIBLE_USER_AUTHZ_CACHE_TTL_MS bounds the responsible-user permission snapshot (default 5000) (#10633).
  • New experimental settings, all off by default: GitHub review bots (enableGitHubReviewBots) shows GitHub bot setup and management (#15416); OpenAI Dot (enableOpenAiDot) adds Dot as an agent choice and requires Assistant connections (MCP), authenticated sign-in, and an HTTPS PAPERCLIP_PUBLIC_URL (#15414); Experimental fast responses (enableFastResponses) reveals Company Settings → Connections and allows acknowledgement comments (#15748). Decision model setup lives under Company Settings → General until fast responses are on (#15473).
  • Review Operator members (#15377): Operators now hold company editing, invitation, connection, tool, and audit grants after startup seeding. Demote members who should not configure agents or connect accounts.
  • Budget policies and unpriced usage (#14997): existing policies get unpricedUsagePolicy: block. If your agents run on providers whose prices Paperclip cannot determine, set the policy to allow or resolve unpriced events through the cost adjustment flow so the budget does not hold them.
  • Custom adapters and managed processes (#15352): managed runs now receive PAPERCLIP_AGENT_KEY_ID, PAPERCLIP_AGENT_PUBLIC_KEY, and PAPERCLIP_AGENT_PRIVATE_KEY; the key values are multiline PEM strings and the private key must not be logged. The wrapping key is PAPERCLIP_SECRETS_MASTER_KEY or the local secrets master-key file; a wrong master key fails the run rather than regenerating the keypair.
  • Private-task callers (#10633): direct reads of a private task by a non-member return 404; owners and admins must pass ?breakGlass=true for an audited emergency read; plugins are non-member principals and see no private content.
  • Slack and GitHub drafts: existing Slack bot drafts without a saved setup method stay on manual setup (#15413); existing GitHub bots, direct webhooks, and manual existing-App recovery keep working, but their settings are hidden until GitHub review bots is enabled (#15416).
  • Harness pins are unchanged for Codex, Claude, and OpenCode. Native Codex now prefers the Codex CLI installed with the server package and tolerates version drift; a sandbox image whose Codex CLI is too old for the selected model is switched to a compatible model with a warning (#15555, #15519).
  • No other configuration or API changes require action.

Contributors

This release has 200 commits from 7 contributors. Thank you to everyone who contributed to this release!

@lorenzozanee, @lusoris

Keep agent work in view while you work elsewhere

  • Keep agent work in view while you work elsewhere. Desktop users can pop the computer view and floating browser into their own windows above other apps, and browser full screen now fills the display.
  • Dictate messages and use workspace commands again. On macOS and Windows, dictation shows your words as you speak, stops when you click the mic again, and keeps words across pauses. On OpenCode v2, / lists workspace commands and skills, and picking one runs it.

Invited teammates can join their workspace during sign-in, invitation emails explain who invited them and where to get help, and completed MCP sign-ins no longer appear to fail. Teams messages and Outlook meeting invitations now wait for your confirmation.

Standalone server and bootstrap installs require Node.js 24.x (24.22.1 or newer), and the bootstrap installer downloads a supported runtime when needed.

v15.0.2v15.0.2 — Stop observer reasoning from consuming the output budget Stable2026-10-23T18:51:46Z

Stop observer reasoning from consuming the output budget

Observer requests to OpenRouter, the cmem.ai gateway, and OpenAI-compatible endpoints now disable reasoning by default, so reasoning tokens no longer fill the output budget and leave a session with zero observations.

  • An empty reply with finish_reason=length is logged and retried once with reasoning forced off. That retry counts against the existing paid-send budget and is bounded by the per-attempt timeout.
  • Billed usage keeps the retry's prompt size and adds completion tokens and cost from both attempts.
  • Health status names the active OpenRouter credential, including a custom OPENROUTER_BASE_URL.
  • OpenAI "Unsupported parameter" responses drop the reasoning field and remember the endpoint. Mandatory-reasoning and invalid-effort refusals are left in place.
  • Empty replies that finish with stop stay accepted.

Ships the observer repair from #5029.

Graphify-Labs/graphify ↗ 1 release · 1 stable
v0.9.95graphify 0.9.95 Stable2026-10-23T17:59:38Z

Twenty-one community pull requests. A security pass on install: the skill-install writes go through randomly-named temp files instead of predictable ones, so a pre-planted symlink can no longer redirect a write. Extraction: Python, Go, C++ and Rust explicit type aliases (and Rust union items) are extracted as type nodes so references resolve instead of minting sourceless stubs, each C# method overload gets its own node bound by argument count, and a package.json dependency's manifest entry links to the node that references it. Plus a one-root-per-repo tree on merged graphs, extended-length cache paths on Windows, and binary media no longer counted as text. The AST cache schema is bumped, so the first build after upgrading re-extracts.

  • Fix: security the skill install stages every write (version stamp, SKILL.md, references) through a randomly-named mkstemp/mkdtemp file created with O_EXCL and restrictive mode instead of a predictable *.tmp name, so a local attacker who pre-creates a symlink at that path can no longer redirect the write to clobber an arbitrary file; the final move stays atomic (#4513, thanks @Mahdifotohi).
  • Fix: python an explicit module-level type alias (X: TypeAlias = ..., type X = ..., NewType) is extracted as a type node, so a field or parameter typed by the alias resolves to it instead of minting a sourceless stub; an implicit assignment, a local alias, or a re-export is left alone (#4578, thanks @madhusudanpatnaik).
  • Fix: go a type A = B alias is extracted as a type node (tree-sitter parses it as a type_alias, not a type_spec), so references resolve to it; a re-export (type Field = pkg.Field) mints no node (#4579, thanks @madhusudanpatnaik).
  • Fix: cpp a namespace-scope using A = B; or typedef B A; alias is extracted as a type node so references resolve; a member alias inside a class and a same-name re-export are excluded (#4580, thanks @madhusudanpatnaik).
  • Fix: rust a type alias and a union item are extracted as type nodes (a union's fields reference their types like a struct), so references resolve instead of minting stubs; an impl-associated type is excluded (#4581, Refs #4285, thanks @madhusudanpatnaik; reported by @jonatasbcardio-boop).
  • Fix: csharp each method overload gets its own node and source location instead of collapsing to one, and a call binds to the overload matching its argument count, across in-file, receiver-typed, bare-name cross-file, partial-class, and interface-dispatch resolution; a non-overloaded method keeps its id (#4584, #4591, thanks @Mpasha17; reported by @TerraVenil).
  • Fix: tree graphify export tree on a merged multi-repo graph gives each repo its own root (keyed by the repo tag) instead of conflating same-path files from different repos; untagged nodes are not counted as a repo (#4524, #4525, thanks @AromalBiju1).
  • Fix: cache AST cache entries are read and written through Windows extended-length (\\?\) paths, so a deep cache path over the 260-character limit no longer fails extraction with a FileNotFoundError; a no-op off Windows (#4542, thanks @omsenjalia).
  • Fix: detect a binary media file (an image or audio/video) is no longer read and counted as text toward the corpus word total; an SVG stays counted as the XML text it is (#4548, thanks @kalkaran).
  • Fix: json_config a package.json dependency's manifest entry links (declares) to the ref node that importing code resolves to, so the manifest entry and its importers share one node instead of being orphaned; the entry is relabelled name@range (#4569, #4572, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah; reported by @BiSide).
  • Feature: yaml .yaml/.yml files are now extracted structurally (a file node plus contains edges to keys) and classified as code rather than documents, so Helm charts, Kubernetes manifests, and CI pipelines contribute nodes to a code-only or --update run instead of nothing, matching how .json is handled. Multi-document streams (--- separators) are walked per document; a data array, an OpenAPI/Swagger spec, a JSON-schema-in-YAML, and a flat data bundle are skipped so data-heavy YAML does not mint orphan nodes; parsing uses safe_load so a !!python/... tag never executes; output is bounded (1 MiB, 500 pairs, depth 6). The AST cache schema is bumped, so the first build after upgrading re-extracts (#2214, #4706, thanks @nothariharan; reported by @dchavezf).
  • Fix: extract a bare call that resolves to a same-named symbol only because the caller imported that symbol's module (from b import other, then a call to a _make_id defined in both a.py and b.py) is no longer promoted to EXTRACTED; the edge is still emitted for connectivity but stays INFERRED, so a symbol that was never imported is not falsely certified. A real symbol import (from a import _make_id) still resolves EXTRACTED (#2945, #4707, thanks @nothariharan; reported by @TotalUnitManagement).
  • Fix: security the SSRF guard blocks a host that resolves to a multicast address (224.0.0.0/4, ff00::/8), closing a gap alongside the existing private/reserved/loopback/link-local checks (#4708, thanks @Dextheking1).
  • Fix: security the Obsidian export sanitizes a node's file-type and confidence before emitting them as frontmatter tags, so a crafted value cannot break out of the YAML list into a sibling key, matching how community tags are already sanitized (#4709, thanks @Dextheking1).
  • Fix: security the Google Workspace shortcut sidecar escapes a file id or url through full YAML double-quoted-scalar escaping (tab, C0/DEL controls, and the Unicode line breaks U+2028/U+2029/U+0085), so a hostile shortcut file cannot inject frontmatter keys (#4710, thanks @Dextheking1).
  • Fix: affected graphify affected <path> resolves a path whose file-node label was disambiguated by the shared-basename suffix pass (for example two hooks.py from different directories), reusing the canonical file-label predicate instead of a bare basename match (#4698, #4713, thanks @Deepjyoti-Sarmah; reported by @karsan8119).
  • Fix: build a raw (--no-cluster) build resolves an import endpoint through the same old-stem alias index the clustered build uses, and mints an external stub only after resolution, so the raw graph no longer freezes an import onto a stub when the clustered graph resolves it (#4670, #4676, thanks @nothariharan; reported by @xiongjianxu).
  • Fix: cross-repo an Objective-C class declared in one repo's header and implemented in another repo's .m binds a member call to the implementation, the cross-repo analog of the same-repo split-dir fix; two same-named classes that both define the selector stay ambiguous (#4690, #4691, thanks @xiongjianxu).
  • Fix: hooks the rebuild hook runs from the checkout's top level (derived from the git common dir, falling back to --show-toplevel), so a stray graphify-out/ in a subdirectory can no longer root the rebuild at the wrong place and walk an enormous tree (#3258, #4689, thanks @jaimemartinez; reported by @dsfaccini).
  • Fix: objc NS_CLOSED_ENUM declarations are extracted as enums with their cases, the same as NS_ENUM/NS_OPTIONS; the AST cache schema is bumped so the first build after upgrading re-extracts (#4705, thanks @Jvxoq).
  • Fix: sql a CREATE TABLE whose column default the SQL grammar cannot parse (for example MySQL/MariaDB DEFAULT current_timestamp()) is recovered from the ERROR node instead of being dropped, so the table and its foreign-key references still resolve; the AST cache schema is bumped (#4613, #4677, thanks @08raviyadav; reported by @AirRunner).

studio-v2.50.0Reasonix Studio v2.50.0 Stable2026-10-23T17:50:03Z

本版让子代理可以在工作台里开成标签页读完整记录，设置里新增导航入口管理、计费方式和放大设置窗口，正文栏可拖宽，并修复多处卡住、显示与对齐问题。

新增

  • 正文栏左右边线可以拖动，两侧同时等量变宽或收窄；缩到“适宜阅读”为止，放到窗口全宽为止，被挡住的侧栏按各自设定的比例让位。关联 #14198 by @imcreazy。
  • 反馈表单的正文可以切到「预览」，先看 Markdown 渲染的样子；公开的议题仍把原文放在代码块里。修复 #14248 fixed in #14255。
  • 设置 → 外观 →「导航入口」可隐藏或调整图标栏和侧栏里的入口，两处同步；会话、反馈、账号和设置始终保留。关联 #14236、#14190。
  • 设置窗口头部多了「放大设置窗口」按钮，可铺满整个窗口、内容区同步变宽；选择会记住，下次打开保持。修复 #14272 fixed in #14271。
  • 桌面端可连自己部署的远程网关（REASONIX_REMOTE_URL、REASONIX_REMOTE_GATEWAY_ID），手机网页按授权里的网关地址连接；非 wss:// 地址会被拒绝。关联 #14282。
  • 从“子代理”面板打开子代理，会在工作台开成标签页，读内核记录的完整对话（运行中持续刷新），工具步骤可折叠、可同时开多个；找不到记录时仍用原对话框。关联 #13523 fixed in #14291。
  • 连接编辑页可选“计费方式”（按量计费或订阅套餐），订阅套餐的用量会按所填价格折算成估算值单独显示，不计入实际花费。关联 #13276。
  • 设置 → 工具与权限第二项提供「AI 文件交付卡片」开关，支持搜索并保存用户选择，重新打开会话生效。关联 #14063 by @SivanCola。

变更

  • 侧栏会记住你折叠过的项目，重新打开界面后仍保持折叠；新项目默认展开，不替你做决定。关联 #14195 by @lancy69。
  • 设置打开时，背后的内容被更深的平面遮罩压下去，设置面板更突出；没有使用实时模糊。关联 #14196 by @lancy69。
  • 正文两侧的拖拽边线常驻一条短细线，看得出这里可以拖；长对话里回到顶部与跳到最新的提示不再一移就消失；两个把手也能用键盘调宽。关联 #14198 by @imcreazy。
  • 隐藏图标栏时，侧栏列出与图标栏相同的入口（文件、工具与权限、扩展、记忆、远程），名称统一；两处读同一份清单。关联 #14236。
  • 并行写入的“乐观模式”现在默认开启：没声明写入范围的子代理和写入不再占住整个工作区；已选过“严格”的不受影响，可在设置里关闭。关联 #14240。
  • 你对某个对话选的“本会话允许”现在随这个对话保存，恢复或重新打开这个对话后不再重复询问；仍只对该对话有效，可随时撤销。关联 #14243。
  • AI 文件交付工具默认开启；已有的显式关闭选择仍然有效。下一次打开会话时增加工具定义，可能产生一次缓存未命中。关联 #14063 by @SivanCola。

修复

  • 工作模式菜单中的 Ask 名称后明确标注“（未实现）”，避免误以为需要额外配置才能启用；现有模式切换和禁用行为保持不变。关联 #14028 fixed in #14093 by @lancy69。
  • 对话栏变窄（如展开工作台）时，输入框底部的按钮条不再折成两行：模式按钮更早收成图标，模型名随栏宽收缩。关联 #14156。
  • 一个会话用到多种货币时，计量条和费用面板不再把不同币种的金额直接相加，而是分币种各显示一个金额。关联 #14178 by @chuiwenwei。
  • 只运行一次的定时任务错过时间后，不再一直显示“运行中”；它会变成“已到期”，不再出现点“续期”提示成功却什么都没运行。关联 #14179 by @chuiwenwei。
  • 终端里对“可能已经跑过”的恢复条目按 r 或 /queue retry 不再重新发送，会说明原因并建议先看对话记录或删除它。关联 #14180 by @chuiwenwei。
  • 导入旧会话时，不再把另一个窗口正打开着的会话搬走或删除；这类会话会留在原处，之后再导入。关联 #14181 by @chuiwenwei。
  • 输入框下方计量条把整个会话的累计花费标成了“本轮”；现在“本会话”显示累计总额，“本轮”只显示最近一轮的花费。关联 #14200。
  • 队列现在由内核拒绝重发“可能已经跑过”的恢复条目，通过接口或 ACP 调用重试时也一样，不会再重复执行同一条指令。关联 #14202。
  • “交付验收”卡片里的长命令不再铺满一大片，只显示开头一行并以省略号结尾，完整命令在鼠标悬停时可见。关联 #14204。
  • 隐藏图标栏时，侧栏各行的图标和文字对齐在同一条竖线上，字号统一为 12px，“新建会话”和“发送反馈”不再加粗。关联 #14207。
  • 设置里“模型可用的工具”列表中，其余内置工具（搜索、读写文件、子代理、记忆、同伴协作等）也按界面语言显示一句话说明，不再露出英文原文。关联 #14208。
  • 在反馈窗口里点过空白处之后，Ctrl+V 粘贴截图不再没反应；剪贴板里以条目形式给出的图片也能贴进去。关联 #14210。
  • 设置窗口加高，菜单在 1080p 屏幕上完整显示、不再出现滚动条；“记忆”图标与文字垂直对齐；空白会话提示和运行分析面板统一称“运行分析”和“运行记录”，不再混称“轨迹”。关联 #14211。
  • 定时运行页现在可以直接信任当前项目，不再要求先去别处点信任；之前点过“暂不信任”或手动选过批准模式、从未看到信任提示的项目也能处理。关联 #14216。
  • 侧栏各行（新建会话、搜索、文件、工具与集成、运行环境、钱包与用量、发送反馈）的文字统一为同一种颜色，“新建会话”不再有底色。关联 #14221。
  • 顶栏「运行分析」的图标换成脉冲线，和旁边的图标一样大、一样粗，不再是偏小的半圆仪表盘。修复 #14222 fixed in #14269。
  • 隐藏图标栏时，侧栏图标对齐项目文件夹，标志对齐行文字；会话分组标签文字上下居中；上面几行去掉提示；账号头像改为单一圆角方块。关联 #14226。
  • 「在文件管理器中显示」按钮换成打开的文件夹图标，不再像分享或外链箭头。关联 #14227。
  • 工作台顶栏里“加宽工作台”按钮移到最左边，“全屏工作台”按钮移到最右边，不再夹在标签中间。关联 #14229。
  • 模型现在知道子代理不是新会话：由它派出、结果回到当前对话、嵌套深度受 max_subagent_depth 限制。关联 #14247。
  • 读取被拒时不再只写“没有权限”：现在说明是哪个路径、它不在会话允许读取的文件夹里，还是在你配置的禁读列表里。关联 #14252。
  • “我的反馈”再次打开时立即显示上次的列表并在后台刷新；等级、账号关联和贡献榜收进一行折叠，点开才加载，不再占满首屏。关联 #14254。
  • 执行过程里调用技能的步骤会写出技能名称，不再只显示 run_skill。关联 #14256 fixed in #14259。
  • 内核拒绝请求后，外壳会检查本次启动的凭据，缺失就立即补回，不必重启 Studio。关联 #14260。
  • 插件的运行时命令不是可执行程序（例如 Windows 上的 .sh 脚本）时，报错直接说明需要提供原生可执行文件，不再只显示系统原话。关联 #14263。
  • 选了与当前实际请求相同的思考强度（如「自动」本就等于「深入」）后，强度按钮立刻显示你的选择，不必退出重进。修复 #14173 fixed in #14265。
  • 付费搜索、网络出站和 MCP 登录的审批卡，「始终允许」下方的说明改为写明它实际记在哪里，不再一律说成权限规则。关联 #14242。
  • 设置里「多个会话同时写一个项目」和「子代理的写入范围」两处的说明改为与新的默认值（乐观模式）一致，不再写「默认严格」。关联 #14240。
  • 模型看到的「派出子代理」工具说明，按新的默认值（乐观模式）描述没声明写入范围的写入，不再说它会占住整个工作区。关联 #14240。
  • 侧栏入口的文字比图标偏高，且“工具与权限”等图标比上面几项更粗更大；现在文字与图标居中，图标粗细大小一致。关联 #14266。
  • 输入完整命令（如 /reload）而旁边有同前缀的更长命令（如 /reload-cmd）时，回车会补全成长命令；现在完整命令排第一，回车直接发送。修复 #14302 fixed in #14304。

升级须知

  • 并行写入的“乐观模式”默认开启，没声明写入范围的子代理不再互相占住整个工作区；想保持原来的严格行为，在设置里关闭。关联 #14240。
  • AI 文件交付工具默认开启，升级后第一次打开会话会因工具定义增加而有一次缓存未命中；想关闭，在设置 → 工具与权限里关掉「AI 文件交付卡片」。关联 #14063 by @SivanCola。

贡献者

感谢本版本的贡献者：@imcreazy、@SivanCola、@lancy69、@chuiwenwei

<!-- lang:en -->

This release opens sub-agents as Workbench tabs with their full record, adds navigation-entry management, a billing choice and an enlarged Settings window, lets you drag the reading column wider, and fixes a number of stalls, display and alignment problems.

New

  • The reading column's edges can be dragged: both sides widen or narrow by the same amount, between the readable measure and the window. Refs #14198 by @imcreazy.
  • the feedback form's body can switch to a Markdown preview; a public issue still shows the original text in a code block. Fixes #14248 fixed in #14255.
  • Settings → Appearance → Navigation entries hides or reorders the shortcuts in the icon rail and sidebar together; sessions, feedback, account and settings stay. Refs #14236, #14190.
  • the settings window has an Enlarge button that fills the whole window and widens its content; the choice is remembered. Fixes #14272 fixed in #14271.
  • the desktop host can use a remote gateway you run (REASONIX_REMOTE_URL, REASONIX_REMOTE_GATEWAY_ID); the phone page follows the grant's gateway; non-wss:// relays are refused. Refs #14282.
  • a sub-agent opened from the Sub-agents panel is now a Workbench tab reading the kernel's full record (live while it runs), foldable, several at once; no record keeps the dialog. Refs #13523 fixed in #14291.
  • the connection editor now has a Billing choice (pay as you go or subscription plan); a plan's usage is shown as a separate estimate at the entered prices, never as money spent. Refs #13276.
  • a searchable AI file delivery switch is the second item in Tools & permissions. It saves your choice for reopened sessions. Refs #14063 by @SivanCola.

Changed

  • the sidebar remembers which projects you folded and keeps them folded when the interface reopens; new projects still start expanded. Refs #14195 by @lancy69.
  • while Settings is open, the content behind it is pushed back by a stronger flat scrim, so Settings stands out; no live blur is used. Refs #14196 by @lancy69.
  • The reading column's edges carry a standing mark, the two pills keep their tip while the pointer moves, and the handles answer the arrow keys. Refs #14198 by @imcreazy.
  • with the icon rail hidden, the sidebar now lists the same destinations as the rail (Files, Tools and permissions, Extensions, Memory, Remote) under the same names, from one list. Refs #14236.
  • optimistic mode for parallel writes is on by default, so writers with no declared scope no longer hold the whole workspace; a saved strict choice is kept. Refs #14240.
  • "Allow for this session" is now saved with its conversation, so resuming or reopening it no longer asks again; it still covers only that conversation and can be revoked. Refs #14243.
  • AI file delivery defaults on; explicit off choices remain off. Newly opened sessions add its tool schema and may incur one cold prefix. Refs #14063 by @SivanCola.

Fixed

  • the work-mode menu now labels the unavailable mode “Ask (Not implemented)” so it does not imply a missing configuration step. Mode switching and Ask's disabled state are unchanged. Refs #14028 fixed in #14093 by @lancy69.
  • with the conversation column narrow (workbench open), the buttons under the composer stay on one row: the mode button collapses sooner and the model name shrinks. Refs #14156.
  • a session billed in more than one currency no longer shows one summed figure under a single symbol; the meter and cost panel show one amount per currency. Refs #14178 by @chuiwenwei.
  • a one-shot scheduled run that missed its time no longer stays Active; it shows as expired, so Renew no longer reports success when nothing will run. Refs #14179 by @chuiwenwei.
  • in the terminal, r and /queue retry no longer re-send a recovered queue entry that may already have run; they say why and suggest checking the transcript or deleting it. Refs #14180 by @chuiwenwei.
  • importing legacy sessions no longer moves or deletes a session that another window has open; it is left in place and settled on a later import. Refs #14181 by @chuiwenwei.
  • the meter under the composer labelled the whole session's spend as "This turn"; it now shows "This session" and the last turn's own amount. Refs #14200.
  • the queue itself now refuses to retry a recovered entry that may already have run, including retries made through the API or ACP, so an instruction is not run twice. Refs #14202.
  • a long command in the delivery receipt card no longer fills the card; it shows its first line with an ellipsis, and the whole command is in the hover text. Refs #14204.
  • with the icon rail hidden, sidebar rows line up icons and labels on one vertical line and share one 12px regular label style; New session and Send feedback are no longer bold. Refs #14207.
  • the settings tool list now describes the remaining built-in tools (search, file edits, sub-agents, memory, peers) in the interface language, not model-facing English. Refs #14208.
  • pasting a screenshot into the feedback form no longer does nothing after clicking a blank part of it, and an image the clipboard offers as an item is taken too. Refs #14210.
  • the settings sheet is taller so its whole menu shows on a 1080p screen, the Memory icon lines up with its label, and the run analysis view keeps one name instead of "trajectory". Refs #14211.
  • the scheduled runs page can trust the open project itself, so a project that never showed the trust prompt, or was declined earlier, no longer leaves you stuck. Refs #14216.
  • the sidebar rows now share one label colour, and New session no longer has a filled background at rest. Refs #14221.
  • the top bar's Run analysis icon is now a pulse line the same size and weight as its neighbours, instead of a small half-circle gauge. Fixes #14222 fixed in #14269.
  • with the rail hidden, sidebar icons match the project folders and the logo the labels; session tabs centre their text; top rows lose hints; the avatar is one rounded square. Refs #14226.
  • the "show in file manager" button now uses an open-folder icon instead of an arrow that read as share or external link. Refs #14227.
  • the workbench bar puts the wide toggle at its left edge and the full-size toggle at its right edge instead of between the tabs. Refs #14229.
  • the model is now told a sub-agent is not a new session: it dispatches it, the answer returns here, and nesting is bounded by max_subagent_depth. Refs #14247.
  • a refused read now says which path was refused and whether it is outside the folders the session may read or on your forbidden-read list, not just "permission denied". Refs #14252.
  • My feedback shows its last list at once and refreshes behind it; level, account and the leaderboard sit behind one collapsed row loaded on open instead of filling the first screen. Refs #14254.
  • a skill step in the execution process now shows which skill it ran instead of just run_skill. Fixes #14256 fixed in #14259.
  • after the kernel refuses a request the shell now checks this launch's credential cookie and restores it if missing, so no relaunch is needed. Refs #14260.
  • when a plugin's runtime command is not an executable program (such as a .sh script on Windows), the error now says the plugin must ship a native executable. Refs #14263.
  • choosing a reasoning depth that sends the same request as the current one (such as High when Auto resolves to High) now shows at once, not after a restart. Fixes #14173 fixed in #14265.
  • on the paid search, network egress and MCP sign-in approval cards, the note under "Always allow" now says where the answer is actually kept instead of calling it a permission rule. Refs #14242.
  • the settings text for sessions writing one project and for sub-agent write scope now matches the new default (optimistic mode) instead of saying "strict by default". Refs #14240.
  • the sub-agent tool's description the model reads now describes writes with no declared scope under the new default (optimistic mode), not as claiming the whole workspace. Refs #14240.
  • sidebar labels sat higher than their icons, and the Tools/Extensions/Memory/Remote icons were bolder and larger than the others; both are now level and matched. Refs #14266.
  • with a command typed in full (/reload) beside longer ones sharing its name (/reload-cmd), Enter completed the longer one; the typed one is now listed first and Enter sends it. Fixes #14302 fixed in #14304.

Upgrade notes

  • Optimistic parallel writes are on by default, so sub-agents that declare no write paths no longer hold the whole workspace; turn it off in Settings to keep the strict behaviour. Refs #14240.
  • The AI file-delivery tool is on by default, so the first session after upgrading has one cache miss; turn it off under Settings, Tools and permissions. Refs #14063 by @SivanCola.

Contributors

macOS 已用 Developer ID 签名并公证，打开时不需要清除隔离属性。Windows 的窗口、内核与安装器都经 Certum 代码签名证书做了 Authenticode 签名。Linux Debian 系从 .deb 安装，Fedora、RHEL、openSUSE 等从 .rpm 安装（sudo dnf install ./ReasonixStudio-linux-amd64.rpm）。x86_64 用文件名带 amd64 的包，aarch64（统信 UOS、麒麟等）用带 arm64 的包。也提供 .AppImage（只提供下载，不会自更新；需要 FUSE 2，或用 --appimage-extract-and-run 启动）。

三个平台都能自更新：Linux 的 .deb 走自己的包（.rpm 的自更新尚未提供，请手动下载新包），Windows 运行下一个安装器，macOS 替换自身 bundle。

career-ops-v1.38.0career-ops v1.38.0: Five Thousand Strong Stable2026-10-23T17:34:18Z

<!-- co:release-notes:career-ops-v1.38.0 --> This release is about not losing what you put in. Your CV, your PDF, your portals.yml, your tracker rows and your saved answers now survive interrupted writes, odd formatting and updates, and it comes from 48 people in one week, in the same days the career-ops Discord passed 5,000 members.

Highlights

  • Updates that keep your files safe. The list of what the updater owns now lives in its own manifest, read without importing, and an install on 1.37.0 updates through a bridge list. Tested before release from 1.37.0 and older installs: apply and rollback left the user files we checked byte-identical. (#5563 by @vliggio)
  • Writes that cannot half-happen. cv.md, portals.yml and the generated PDF are replaced atomically, and every core lock now uses one protocol. (#5552, #5389 by @vliggio)
  • Batch, more in your hands. --company limits a run to the companies you name, --thin-action decides what happens when no JD text could be fetched, and workers apply your dealbreakers and record a finished SKIP. (#5526, #5547 by @zhangruyi1993, #5493 by @mbrow190)
  • More places to look. Computrabajo and Magneto365 for Latin America (#2650 by @configurowebmax), Atlassian (#5497 by @kellymmcgrath), Dover (#5565 by @IaroslavMazur), Zoho Recruit career sites (#5345 by @ilyakanevskiy) and white-label SuccessFactors sites in scan:full (#5740 by @Schlaflied).
  • Following up, with less to remember. A duplicate check before you write a CV (#5735), take-home deadlines (#5736), interview invites read from an .ics file (#5744), all by @Schlaflied, and tracker.mjs query --csv for your spreadsheet (#5624 by @mbrow190).

Security

  • The web app's assisted apply could submit an application form when the text it typed contained a line break: line breaks are now removed from that text, and the fallback inserts it without pressing keys, so it no longer submits the form (GHSA-rm8h-2825-ww26, reported by @vliggio, #5770).

Updating

Run node update-system.mjs apply --confirm in your career-ops folder. If you said no to the update prompt earlier, this is the same command.

Thank you

This release carries 300 pull requests from 48 people, 17 of them contributing for the first time.
